Mind, intellect, ego, consciousness, and likewise the individual self, / driven by the wind, then quickly depart from the body. // 40
Another, subtle body, acquired previously, then comes into being for it; / joined there, that individual self once again remains deluded. // 41
Such indeed is this condition of the host of all living beings brought about by time; / without yoga, the subtle state belonging to Maheśvara cannot be won. // 42
Seated or asleep, having practiced restraint regarding departure, / knowing the thread [to be] Maheśvara, he is liberated at will, O Vyāsa. // 43

7.19.m:
The sage should then hold a razor, an axe, or a trident; / then all his modifications dissolve along with the sense-faculties. // 44
And he perceives Īśvara, the twenty-sixth principle, Brahman residing in his own body; / [whereas] to a dying creature, the dull mind brings fierce [pain]. // 45
Overwhelmed by delusion due to pain, he does not find the real entity of knowledge. / Through this rite, O brahmin, free from all sickness, // 46
one easily ascends to Brahman as if onto the roof of a mansion from the ground. / Having understood the five categories, firmly grounded in the end of suffering, // 47
purified by the five Brahmans, initiated with ash, the twice-born / yogin whose mind is solely on Śaṅkara attains this knowledge. // 48
Without undertaking the Śāṅkara observance, they do not attain even with effort / this Maheśvara yoga, which is partless and the cause of liberation. // 49
Therefore, practicing the Pāśupata observance, O Vyāsa of great intellect, / being devoted to Mahādeva, attain this knowledge! // 50
Other yogins do not thus attain this supreme Brahman, / except those Śiva-yogins who have sought refuge in Mahādeva. // 51

This entire rule of liberation, devoid of all conventional cognition / [and] partless, has been spoken, O Vyāsa, beyond which nothing higher exists. // 52
Thus Pāśupata brahmins, having entered that partless Maheśvara / through yoga, are liberated, freed from rebirth. // 53
I shall describe the divine abode of the manifest [Lord], situated beyond the world of Brahmā, / where those devoted to Mahādeva go. // 54
Thus ends the one hundred and eighty-second chapter in the Skandapurāṇa, in the exposition of Pāśupata yoga, on the rule of yoga.

7.19.m:
Sanatkumāra said:
Situated above the seven [worlds]—Satya, Mahas, / Jana, and Tapas, as well as those of the future, past, and present— // 1
is the world of the blessed Śambhu, where the manifest Śiva abides. / It cannot be indicated by reasoning; the worlds are established within it. // 2
Above, horizontally, and below, the worlds are bound to it. / The entire cosmic egg is established in that Śivaloka. // 3
It does not perish at the dissolution, constant, immovable, the abode of the gods, / where I, Sanaka and others, Brahmā the Grandsire, // 4
led by the Bālakhilyas, and the perfected ones like Kapila, / having attained Śivayoga, free from qualities such as sattva, // 5
remain blissful, O Vyāsa, serving that Lord. / The Lord is an ultimate subtle particle, accessible through devotion to the wise. // 6
Endowed with supreme sovereignty, the Lord of forms abides there. / Forbearance, truth, firmness, austerity, and detachment, // 7

Śaiva powers characterized by the authority of knowledge, / from which he produced the two supreme lords, the progenitors Brahmā and Viṣṇu. // 13
To those two, who had become [his] material instruments, he gave supreme creatorship. / Imperishable, stainless, subtle, partless, and yet with parts, // 14
standing in a stable, formed, transcendent, divine, atomic state; / prior to the mind, at the beginning of darkness, that manifestation of his splendor arose. // 15
The golden egg which existed, both worldly and leading to emancipation, / that great, everywhere eternal principle then arose from Īśvara. // 16
From that splitting of the seed, he is considered the all-pervading knower of the field. / The nature called Vaiṣṇavī also came forth from him. // 17
For the sake of creating gods, asuras, and the rest, she assumed the state of Brahmā. / From the splitting of the egg of the lotus-born Brahmā, who is of the nature of Śaṃkara, / and in front of the world of Brahmā, is that great city made of light, // 18
which is the abode of the Lord of forms, Īśvara, the supreme Self, / named Śivapura, O Vyāsa, the goal of the yogins devoted to the Lord. // 19

Surrounded by a great rampart made of gold, / having the form of the shining sun, with splendor greater than fire, // 21

Adorned with banners shining like rays of the moon and elsewhere having the form of sunbeams, / it shone resplendent, offering pleasant breezes. / That city, strewn with trees resembling mountains, / shone with varied flowers of all seasons and desire-yielding gem-fruits. / Just as Meru among mountains is the supreme and great, / even so that city shone, situated above all the worlds. / There Hara, the Lord of All, directly the master of the great elements, / the twenty-sixth Parameśvara, always dwells together with his wife.
Lakṣmī, Medhā, Dhṛti, Hrī, Śrī, Kīrti, and Sarasvatī, / the mothers of the worlds, rejoice there together with Umā.
Those men whose souls are offered in Śiva-consciousness, who are devoted to Rudra, / wherever they die, my child, their abode is said to be there. / And those Māheśvaras, O Vyāsa, who dwell in the abode of Śaṅkara, / the sages devoted to Śaṅkara—hear about them with a focused mind:

Through veneration, one may obtain the highest attainment of yoga and supreme liberation. / O bulls among brahmins, [hearing] this primordial, holy and supreme hymn of praise to the lord of Umā, / and the narration of the great majesty of the Goddess, combined with all the sacred scriptures, / along with the birth and exploits of Skanda […] / […] they would attain […]. / By whichever lords of serpents, kings of asuras, yakṣas, gods, siddhas, and lords of brahmins / this has been revered, with hearts yielding all existence to Śambhu, / they all, possessing bodies bright as the blazing sun and fire, three-eyed, shining like the moon, / shone as followers of the god and excellent attendants […].

7.20.m: Table of Contents
1. In the first chapter:

7.20.s: prayāge ṛṣīṇāṃ sūtena samāgamaḥ, ṛṣīṇāṃ skandajanmaviṣayakaḥ praśnaḥ . sūtasya byāsasanatkumārasaṃvādamukhena skandotpattikathāvataraṇopakramaḥ .
7.20.d: प्रयागे ऋषीणां सूतेन समागमः, ऋषीणां स्कन्दजन्मविषयकः प्रश्नः . सूतस्य ब्याससनत्कुमारसंवादमुखेन स्कन्दोत्पत्तिकथावतरणोपक्रमः .
7.20.m: The meeting of the seers with Sūta at Prayāga; the seers' inquiry regarding the birth of Skanda; the beginning of Sūta's recitation of the story of the birth of Skanda through the dialogue between Vyāsa and Sanatkumāra.
2. In the second chapter:
Sanatkumāra's promise to Vyāsa to narrate the ancient story concerning the birth of Skanda; and a brief summary of the topics contained in the Purāṇa itself.
3. In the third chapter:

7.20.s: śambhuto brahmaṇa utpattiḥ, tapaścaryā, śarvadarśanam, varalābhaḥ, prājāpatye 'bhiṣekaśca .
7.20.d: शम्भुतो ब्रह्मण उत्पत्तिः, तपश्चर्या, शर्वदर्शनम्, वरलाभः, प्राजापत्ये ऽभिषेकश्च .
7.20.m: The origin of Brahmā from Śambhu; the practice of austerity; the vision of Śarva; the obtaining of the boon; and the consecration to the office of lord of creatures (Prajāpati).
4. In the fourth chapter:

7.20.s: prajāsṛṣṭyarthaṃ brahmaṇaḥ punastapaścaraṇam . rudrādvaraprāptiḥ, putrakāmanayāgnau havirjuhvato brahmaṇo lalāṭajasvedasaṃsa- rgādagnito nīlalohitarudrasyotpattiḥ, dakṣadharmādīnāmutpattiḥ, krameṇa sakalaprajāsṛṣṭiḥ, kālāntare tasya (brahmaṇaḥ) visarjanam, prayāge yajato marīcyādiṣaṭkulīyānāmṛṣīṇāmāgamaḥ, samāgatānāṃ teṣāṃ sarvajaganniyantṛparamakāraṇa- jijñāsayā praśnaḥ, brahmaṇā rudrasyaiva sarvajaganniyantṛparamakāraṇatvakathanam, taddarśanārthaṃ ca mahāsatrānuṣṭhānopadeśaḥ, brahmaṇā cakrasya virjanam, naimiśotpattiḥ .
7.20.d: प्रजासृष्ट्यर्थं ब्रह्मणः पुनस्तपश्चरणम् . रुद्राद्वरप्राप्तिः, पुत्रकामनयाग्नौ हविर्जुह्वतो ब्रह्मणो ललाटजस्वेदसंस- र्गादग्नितो नीललोहितरुद्रस्योत्पत्तिः, दक्षधर्मादीनामुत्पत्तिः, क्रमेण सकलप्रजासृष्टिः, कालान्तरे तस्य (ब्रह्मणः) विसर्जनम्, प्रयागे यजतो मरीच्यादिषट्कुलीयानामृषीणामागमः, समागतानां तेषां सर्वजगन्नियन्तृपरमकारण- जिज्ञासया प्रश्नः, ब्रह्मणा रुद्रस्यैव सर्वजगन्नियन्तृपरमकारणत्वकथनम्, तद्दर्शनार्थं च महासत्रानुष्ठानोपदेशः, ब्रह्मणा चक्रस्य विर्जनम्, नैमिशोत्पत्तिः .
7.20.m: Brahmā's practicing of austerity once more for the sake of creating progeny; the obtaining of a boon from Rudra; the birth of the dark-red (Nīlalohita) Rudra from the fire due to contact with the sweat arising on Brahmā's forehead as he offered oblations into the fire desiring a son; the birth of Dakṣa, Dharma, and others; the gradual creation of all creatures; in the course of time, his (Brahmā's) departure; the arrival of the seers belonging to the six lineages, Marīci and others, who were sacrificing at Prayāga; the inquiry by those who had assembled out of a desire to know the supreme cause and controller of the entire world; Brahmā's declaration that Rudra alone is the supreme cause and controller of the entire world, and his instruction to perform a great sacrificial session in order to see him; Brahmā's release of the wheel; the origin of Naimiṣa.
5. In the fifth chapter:

7.20.s: naimiśe ṛṣīṇāṃ dīrghasatrārambhaḥ . tatra vāyorāgamanam, jagatsṛṣṭyādiviṣaye praśnaḥ, vāyunā tatsarvasyāśeṣatayā kathanam . satrasamāptau vedīmadhyāt sarasvatyāḥ prādurbhāvaḥ . nadīrūpeṇa pravṛttāyāṃ tasyāmṛṣīṇāmavabhṛthasnānam, brahmalokavibhūṣaṇāyāḥ sarasvatyā itthaṃ tatovatīrya bhūrloke pravṛttau kiṃ kāraṇamiti ṛṣīṇāṃ praśnaḥ, brahmayajña- vivādarūpapurātanetihāsavivaraṇamukhena vāyukṛtattatkathāvatāraḥ, svakṛtalokasṛṣṭidarśanād brahmaṇaḥ sarvaśreṣṭha- tvābhimānaḥ, brahmayajñayorvivādaḥ, rudrasya tatra prārdubhāvaḥ, kruddhasya brahmaṇaḥ paṃcamaśīrṣotpattiḥ, rudrakṛtaṃ tatkṛntanam, brahmakṛtā rudrastutiḥ, kṛtasya śiraso dhāraṇārthaṃ prārthanā ca .
7.20.d: नैमिशे ऋषीणां दीर्घसत्रारम्भः . तत्र वायोरागमनम्, जगत्सृष्ट्यादिविषये प्रश्नः, वायुना तत्सर्वस्याशेषतया कथनम् . सत्रसमाप्तौ वेदीमध्यात् सरस्वत्याः प्रादुर्भावः . नदीरूपेण प्रवृत्तायां तस्यामृषीणामवभृथस्नानम्, ब्रह्मलोकविभूषणायाः सरस्वत्या इत्थं ततोवतीर्य भूर्लोके प्रवृत्तौ किं कारणमिति ऋषीणां प्रश्नः, ब्रह्मयज्ञ- विवादरूपपुरातनेतिहासविवरणमुखेन वायुकृतत्तत्कथावतारः, स्वकृतलोकसृष्टिदर्शनाद् ब्रह्मणः सर्वश्रेष्ठ- त्वाभिमानः, ब्रह्मयज्ञयोर्विवादः, रुद्रस्य तत्र प्रार्दुभावः, क्रुद्धस्य ब्रह्मणः पंचमशीर्षोत्पत्तिः, रुद्रकृतं तत्कृन्तनम्, ब्रह्मकृता रुद्रस्तुतिः, कृतस्य शिरसो धारणार्थं प्रार्थना च .
7.20.m: In Naimiṣa, the commencement of the long sacrificial session by the seers. The arrival of Vāyu there; the question regarding the creation of the universe and related matters; the complete narration of all that by Vāyu. At the completion of the sacrificial session, the appearance of Sarasvatī from the middle of the sacrificial altar. The final ritual ablution (avabhṛthasnāna) of the seers in her as she flows in the form of a river; the question of the seers as to what caused Sarasvatī, the ornament of the realm of Brahmā, to descend from there and flow in the mortal world; the introduction to that story given by Vāyu through recounting the ancient historical account of the dispute between Brahmā and Yajña; Brahmā's conceit of supremacy upon beholding his own creation of the worlds; the dispute between Brahmā and Yajña; the appearance of Rudra there; the sprouting of a fifth head of the enraged Brahmā; the cutting off of that [head] by Rudra; the hymn of praise to Rudra made by Brahmā, and the entreaty for carrying the severed head.
6. In the sixth chapter:

7.20.s: brahmaṇo'nurodhāt tacchiraḥkapālamādāya vikṛtarūpaṃ dadhato rudrasya devaveśmasu bhikṣārthaṃ pracāraḥ, viṣṇoḥ sakāśād bhikṣāmādadānena rudreṇa kapālavartini bhaikṣarase viṣṇośchāyādarśanāttatsadṛśamūrtternarasya sarjanam .
7.20.d: ब्रह्मणोऽनुरोधात् तच्छिरःकपालमादाय विकृतरूपं दधतो रुद्रस्य देववेश्मसु भिक्षार्थं प्रचारः, विष्णोः सकाशाद् भिक्षामाददानेन रुद्रेण कपालवर्तिनि भैक्षरसे विष्णोश्छायादर्शनात्तत्सदृशमूर्त्तेर्नरस्य सर्जनम् .
7.20.m: At the request of Brahmā, Rudra, taking the skull of that head and assuming a deformed form, wanders about the dwellings of the gods for alms; while receiving alms from Viṣṇu, Rudra beholds the reflection of Viṣṇu in the alms-broth resting in the skull, and from that creates Nara whose form resembles him.
7. In the seventh chapter:

7.20.s: dhṛtakapālamṛya bhairavarūpiṇo rudrasya bhaikṣārthaṃ tato brahālokagamanam, tatromiti vyāharatastasya vadanāt sarasvatyāḥ prādurbhāvaḥ, kapālasaṃsthāpanam, mahiṣarūpiṇo hālāhalāhvayasyāsurasya vināśaḥ, kapālamātṝṇāmutpattiḥ, mahākapālasarasastotrasya cotpattiḥ .
7.20.d: धृतकपालमृय भैरवरूपिणो रुद्रस्य भैक्षार्थं ततो ब्रहालोकगमनम्, तत्रोमिति व्याहरतस्तस्य वदनात् सरस्वत्याः प्रादुर्भावः, कपालसंस्थापनम्, महिषरूपिणो हालाहलाह्वयस्यासुरस्य विनाशः, कपालमातॄणामुत्पत्तिः, महाकपालसरसस्तोत्रस्य चोत्पत्तिः .
7.20.m: Rudra in the form of Bhairava, carrying the skull, goes from there to the realm of Brahmā for alms; while he utters 'Om' there, the manifestation of Sarasvatī from his mouth; the placing down of the skull; the destruction of the demon named Hālāhala who took the form of a buffalo; the origin of the skull-Mothers; and the origin of the praise of the Great Skull Lake.
8. In the eighth chapter:

7.20.s: sarasvatīpravṛttikathosaṃhāraḥ . satrasamāptau brahmaṇastatrāgamaḥ, brahmaṇa upadeśād ṛṣibhiḥ śaṃkarārādhanoddeśena punarbahuvidhasatrānuṣṭhānasamārabhaṇam . satre svarbhānunā somasyāpaharaṇam, gāyatryā śyenībhūya tatpratyānayanam, satra- samāptiḥ . brahmādidevānāmṛṣibhiḥ saha maināke tapaścaryā, tapaso'nte tuṣṭena śaṃkareṇa tebhyo darśanadānam .
7.20.d: सरस्वतीप्रवृत्तिकथोसंहारः . सत्रसमाप्तौ ब्रह्मणस्तत्रागमः, ब्रह्मण उपदेशाद् ऋषिभिः शंकराराधनोद्देशेन पुनर्बहुविधसत्रानुष्ठानसमारभणम् . सत्रे स्वर्भानुना सोमस्यापहरणम्, गायत्र्या श्येनीभूय तत्प्रत्यानयनम्, सत्र- समाप्तिः . ब्रह्मादिदेवानामृषिभिः सह मैनाके तपश्चर्या, तपसोऽन्ते तुष्टेन शंकरेण तेभ्यो दर्शनदानम् .
7.20.m: The conclusion of the story of the descent of Sarasvatī. At the completion of the sacrificial session, the arrival of Brahmā there; by the instruction of Brahmā, the seers commence once again the performance of various sacrificial sessions with the aim of propitiating Śaṃkara. In the sacrifice, the abduction of Soma by Svarbhānu; Gāyatrī becoming a female hawk and bringing it back; the conclusion of the sacrifice. The performance of austerity on Mount Maināka by Brahmā and the other gods together with the seers; at the end of the austerity, Śaṃkara, being pleased, grants them his darśana.
9. In the ninth chapter:

7.20.s: brahmādikṛtā rudrastutiḥ, teṣu rudrasyānugrahaḥ . rudreṇa svatejaso visarjanam . tejasordhāṃśena mukhata ulkāsarjanam . rudrādeśānnārībhūtāyāstasyā brahmaṇa arādhanāya tapaścaraṇam . svarṇākṣa-svarṇākṣīnāmasamākhyā . ṣaṭkulīyānāṃ tatraiva kṣetre nivasanārthamādeśaḥ, kṣetramahimā .
7.20.d: ब्रह्मादिकृता रुद्रस्तुतिः, तेषु रुद्रस्यानुग्रहः . रुद्रेण स्वतेजसो विसर्जनम् . तेजसोर्धांशेन मुखत उल्कासर्जनम् . रुद्रादेशान्नारीभूतायास्तस्या ब्रह्मण अराधनाय तपश्चरणम् . स्वर्णाक्ष-स्वर्णाक्षीनामसमाख्या . षट्कुलीयानां तत्रैव क्षेत्रे निवसनार्थमादेशः, क्षेत्रमहिमा .
7.20.m: The hymn of praise to Rudra offered by Brahmā and the others; Rudra's grace upon them. Rudra's release of his own fiery splendor. The emission of a meteor from his mouth with half of that splendor. By Rudra's command, the practice of austerity by her who had become a woman, in order to propitiate Brahmā. The appellation of the names Svarṇākṣa and Svarṇākṣī. The command to the seers of the six lineages to dwell right in that sacred field; the greatness of the sacred field.
10. In the tenth chapter:

7.20.s: rudrājñayā tapaścarantyāstasyā devyā brahmaṇa upadeśāt tryambakapatiprāptaye dakṣaduhitṛtvena satīnāmnā śarīrāntara- (janma) grahaṇam, satyāstryambakabhāryātvam, rudrāṇāṃ sṛṣṭiḥ, sthāṇupadaniruktiḥ, dakṣakṛtaḥ satyā avamānaḥ, satyā yogadhāraṇayā dehatyāgaḥ, mahādevakṛto dakṣaśāpaḥ .
7.20.d: रुद्राज्ञया तपश्चरन्त्यास्तस्या देव्या ब्रह्मण उपदेशात् त्र्यम्बकपतिप्राप्तये दक्षदुहितृत्वेन सतीनाम्ना शरीरान्तर- (जन्म) ग्रहणम्, सत्यास्त्र्यम्बकभार्यात्वम्, रुद्राणां सृष्टिः, स्थाणुपदनिरुक्तिः, दक्षकृतः सत्या अवमानः, सत्या योगधारणया देहत्यागः, महादेवकृतो दक्षशापः .
7.20.m: By the instruction of Brahmā, that goddess who was performing austerity by Rudra's command assumes another bodily birth under the name Satī as the daughter of Dakṣa in order to obtain Tryambaka as her husband; Satī becomes the wife of Tryambaka; the creation of the Rudras; the etymological explanation of the word Sthāṇu; the dishonor shown to Satī by Dakṣa; the abandonment of her body by Satī through the practice of yoga; the curse laid upon Dakṣa by Mahādeva.
11. In the eleventh chapter:

7.20.s: kadācid himavato gṛhe kaśpasyāgamaḥ . loke khyātikaraṃ pūjyatvāpādakaṃ ca kiṃ, kena cākṣayā lokāḥ syuriti kaśyapa prati himavataḥ praśnaḥ, apatyena sarvamāpyata iti kaśyapakṛtamapatyamahimavarṇanam, dṛṣṭāntamukhena ca sukeśopākhyānakathanam . sukeśasya rudrārādhanayā gaṇapatvaprāptistatpitṝṇāṃ gartāduddharaṇaṃ ceti . kaśyapasya himavantaṃ prati guṇavadapatyotpādanopadeśaḥ, himavatastapaścaraṇam . brahmaṇo varaprāptiḥ . menāyāṃ kanyātrayotpādanam trikumārīṇāṃ duścaratapaścaraṇam, aparṇādi nāma-nirvacanam prasaṅgāt tāsāṃ patiputrādisamullekhaḥ . umāyā mahādeva-patiprāptaye tapaścaraṇam, brahmaṇā samāśvāsanaṃ varadānaṃ ca .
7.20.d: कदाचिद् हिमवतो गृहे कश्पस्यागमः . लोके ख्यातिकरं पूज्यत्वापादकं च किं, केन चाक्षया लोकाः स्युरिति कश्यप प्रति हिमवतः प्रश्नः, अपत्येन सर्वमाप्यत इति कश्यपकृतमपत्यमहिमवर्णनम्, दृष्टान्तमुखेन च सुकेशोपाख्यानकथनम् . सुकेशस्य रुद्राराधनया गणपत्वप्राप्तिस्तत्पितॄणां गर्तादुद्धरणं चेति . कश्यपस्य हिमवन्तं प्रति गुणवदपत्योत्पादनोपदेशः, हिमवतस्तपश्चरणम् . ब्रह्मणो वरप्राप्तिः . मेनायां कन्यात्रयोत्पादनम् त्रिकुमारीणां दुश्चरतपश्चरणम्, अपर्णादि नाम-निर्वचनम् प्रसङ्गात् तासां पतिपुत्रादिसमुल्लेखः . उमाया महादेव-पतिप्राप्तये तपश्चरणम्, ब्रह्मणा समाश्वासनं वरदानं च .
7.20.m: Once, the arrival of Kaśyapa at the abode of Himavat. Himavat's question to Kaśyapa: 'What brings renown in the world and confers worshipfulness, and by what may worlds become imperishable?'; Kaśyapa's description of the greatness of offspring, that everything is obtained through offspring, and the narration of the episode of Sukeśa by way of illustration. Sukeśa's attainment of the rank of gaṇa through the propitiation of Rudra, and the raising of his ancestors from the pit. Kaśyapa's advice to Himavat to produce virtuous offspring; Himavat's practice of austerity. The obtaining of a boon from Brahmā. The generation of three daughters upon Menā; the three maidens' practice of severe austerities; the etymological explanation of names such as Aparṇā; in this connection, the mention of their husbands, sons, and so forth. Umā's practice of austerity to obtain Mahādeva as her husband; Brahmā's consolation and granting of a boon.
12. In the twelfth chapter:

7.20.s: brahmaṇaḥ samāśvāsanena devyāstapaso nivṛttiḥ . svāśramādvāri jātamaśokaṃ samāśritya saṃsthitāyāṃ devyāḥ samakṣaṃ śaśāṅkatilakasya śivasya vikṛtabrāhmaṇarūpeṇopasthitirvivāhārthaṃ prārthanā ca . devyāḥ svasyāsvatantratvajñāpanam . tadarthaṃ pinturantikaṃ gantumanurodhaḥ . śivasya tenaiva rūpeṇa himālayasamīpe gamanaṃ kanyāyācanaṃ ca . himālayena , tatra sā svecchayā yaṃ tasyā bharttā bhave'ditisvābhiprāyapraka- --- tataḥ pratyāgatya nairāśyaṃ prakaṭayataḥ śivasya skandhe 'śokastabakasaṃsthāpanena tadaiva devyā tasya svato varaṇam, tato'ntarhitasya śivasya punardevyā agrato grāhagrastadīnabrāhmaṇabaṭurūpeṇa narmalīlāpradarśanam .
7.20.d: ब्रह्मणः समाश्वासनेन देव्यास्तपसो निवृत्तिः . स्वाश्रमाद्वारि जातमशोकं समाश्रित्य संस्थितायां देव्याः समक्षं शशाङ्कतिलकस्य शिवस्य विकृतब्राह्मणरूपेणोपस्थितिर्विवाहार्थं प्रार्थना च . देव्याः स्वस्यास्वतन्त्रत्वज्ञापनम् . तदर्थं पिन्तुरन्तिकं गन्तुमनुरोधः . शिवस्य तेनैव रूपेण हिमालयसमीपे गमनं कन्यायाचनं च . हिमालयेन , तत्र सा स्वेच्छया यं तस्या भर्त्ता भवेऽदितिस्वाभिप्रायप्रक- --- ततः प्रत्यागत्य नैराश्यं प्रकटयतः शिवस्य स्कन्धे ऽशोकस्तबकसंस्थापनेन तदैव देव्या तस्य स्वतो वरणम्, ततोऽन्तर्हितस्य शिवस्य पुनर्देव्या अग्रतो ग्राहग्रस्तदीनब्राह्मणबटुरूपेण नर्मलीलाप्रदर्शनम् .
7.20.m: The cessation of the goddess's austerity through the consolation of Brahmā. As the goddess stands leaning against an aśoka tree that grew by the door of her own hermitage, the appearance of Śiva, whose mark is the crescent moon, in the guise of a deformed brahmin before her, and his proposal for marriage. The goddess's declaration of her lack of independence. The request that he go to her father for that purpose. Śiva's going to the presence of Himālaya in that very guise and begging for the maiden. Himālaya's disclosure of his own view that 'there, he whom she chooses by her own free will shall be her husband'— / then, upon Śiva returning and displaying despair, the goddess immediately chooses him of her own accord by placing an aśoka blossom-cluster upon his shoulder; then, Śiva disappears and again displays playful sport before the goddess in the form of a miserable young brahmin seized by a crocodile.
13. In the thirteenth chapter:

7.20.s: himavatpṛṣṭhe devyāḥ svayaṃvaramahotsavaḥ . salokapālānāṃ sagaṇānāṃ tridivaukasāṃ gandharvayakṣoragakinnarādīnāṃ ca samakṣaṃ devyā mahādevapativaraṇam . udvāhārthaṃ tatra maṇḍapanirmāṇam . ṛtūnāṃ vicitra samāgamaḥ . sarvabhūtasamājo- pasthitiḥ brahmaṇa ārtvijye pārvatīparameśvarayorvevāhikavidhisamāpattiḥ .
7.20.d: हिमवत्पृष्ठे देव्याः स्वयंवरमहोत्सवः . सलोकपालानां सगणानां त्रिदिवौकसां गन्धर्वयक्षोरगकिन्नरादीनां च समक्षं देव्या महादेवपतिवरणम् . उद्वाहार्थं तत्र मण्डपनिर्माणम् . ऋतूनां विचित्र समागमः . सर्वभूतसमाजो- पस्थितिः ब्रह्मण आर्त्विज्ये पार्वतीपरमेश्वरयोर्वेवाहिकविधिसमापत्तिः .
7.20.m: The great festival of the goddess's svayaṃvara on the ridge of Himavat. In the presence of the guardians of the quarters, the celestial hosts, the dwellers of heaven, and the gandharvas, yakṣas, serpents, kinnaras, and others, the goddess chooses Mahādeva as her husband. The construction of a pavilion there for the wedding. The marvelous assembly of the seasons. The arrival of the gathering of all beings; with Brahmā acting as the officiating priest, the completion of the wedding rites of Pārvatī and Parameśvara.
14. In the fourteenth chapter:

7.20.s: udvāhānantaraṃ harṣātiśayena brahmādibhiḥ kṛtāḥ devadevastutiḥ . tuṣṭasya śambhordevānprati varaditsā . varasya samucitakālāvadhi tathaiva nyāsārthaṃ devānāmanurodhaḥ . śivena tasyānumodanam .
7.20.d: उद्वाहानन्तरं हर्षातिशयेन ब्रह्मादिभिः कृताः देवदेवस्तुतिः . तुष्टस्य शम्भोर्देवान्प्रति वरदित्सा . वरस्य समुचितकालावधि तथैव न्यासार्थं देवानामनुरोधः . शिवेन तस्यानुमोदनम् .
7.20.m: After the wedding, the praise of the God of gods offered by Brahmā and the others with supreme joy. The desire of the pleased Śambhu to grant boons to the gods. The gods' request to keep the boon as a deposit until the suitable time. The approval of that by Śiva.
15. In the fifteenth chapter:

7.20.s: manmathasya durabhiprāyaḥ . devadevakṛto manmathadehadāhaḥ . devadevyo ratisamāśvāsanam . vasiṣṭhasya tapaścaryā . devadevadarśanam, vasiṣṭhakṛtā devadevastutiḥ . devadevasya tasminnanugrahaḥ, varadānam .
7.20.d: मन्मथस्य दुरभिप्रायः . देवदेवकृतो मन्मथदेहदाहः . देवदेव्यो रतिसमाश्वासनम् . वसिष्ठस्य तपश्चर्या . देवदेवदर्शनम्, वसिष्ठकृता देवदेवस्तुतिः . देवदेवस्य तस्मिन्ननुग्रहः, वरदानम् .
7.20.m: The evil intention of Manmatha. The burning of Manmatha's body by the God of gods. The consolation of Rati by the God and Goddess. The practice of austerity by Vasiṣṭha. The darśana of the God of gods; the praise of the God of gods made by Vasiṣṭha. The grace of the God of gods toward him, and the granting of a boon.
16. In the sixteenth chapter:

7.20.s: vasiṣṭhāt śakterutpattiḥ . apatyārthaṃ śaktestapaścaryā . abhīṣṭavaralābhaḥ, śakteḥ patnyā adṛśyantyā garbhadhāraṇam . garbhavatyāṃ lasyāṃ kalmāṣapādena rājñā guruśāpādrakṣobhāvamāpannena śakterbhakṣaṇam .
7.20.d: वसिष्ठात् शक्तेरुत्पत्तिः . अपत्यार्थं शक्तेस्तपश्चर्या . अभीष्टवरलाभः, शक्तेः पत्न्या अदृश्यन्त्या गर्भधारणम् . गर्भवत्यां लस्यां कल्माषपादेन राज्ञा गुरुशापाद्रक्षोभावमापन्नेन शक्तेर्भक्षणम् .
7.20.m: The birth of Śakti from Vasiṣṭha. Śakti's practice of austerity for the sake of offspring. The attainment of the desired boon; the conception by Śakti's wife Adṛśyantī. While she was pregnant, the devouring of Śakti by King Kalmāṣapāda, who had fallen into the state of a rakṣas due to the curse of a guru.
17. In the seventeenth chapter:

7.20.s: rājñā kalmāṣapādena śakterbhakṣaṇe kiṃ kāraṇaṃ kimarthaṃ ca rājā rakṣasāviṣṭa iti vyāsakṛtajijñāsāśamanārtha puna- rvistareṇa saudāsopākhyānārambhaḥ . tatra viśvāmitrapreritena rakṣasā hṛtacetanena rājñā māṃsabhojanārthine guruputrāya śaktaye manuṣyamāṃsapariveṣaṇam . tadvijñāya kruddhena muninā rājñe puruṣādo ( rākṣaso) bhaviṣyasīti śāpadānam . mohitena ca rājñā 'tvāmeva prathamaṃ sabhrātṛkaṃ bhakṣayiṣyāmī'ti pratijñānam .
7.20.d: राज्ञा कल्माषपादेन शक्तेर्भक्षणे किं कारणं किमर्थं च राजा रक्षसाविष्ट इति व्यासकृतजिज्ञासाशमनार्थ पुन- र्विस्तरेण सौदासोपाख्यानारम्भः . तत्र विश्वामित्रप्रेरितेन रक्षसा हृतचेतनेन राज्ञा मांसभोजनार्थिने गुरुपुत्राय शक्तये मनुष्यमांसपरिवेषणम् . तद्विज्ञाय क्रुद्धेन मुनिना राज्ञे पुरुषादो ( राक्षसो) भविष्यसीति शापदानम् . मोहितेन च राज्ञा ऽत्वामेव प्रथमं सभ्रातृकं भक्षयिष्यामीऽति प्रतिज्ञानम् .
7.20.m: To appease the inquiry made by Vyāsa as to what was the reason for Śakti being devoured by King Kalmāṣapāda and why the king was possessed by a demon, the beginning of the narrative of Saudāsa [is recounted] once more in detail: There, by the king whose senses were deranged by a demon dispatched by Viśvāmitra, human flesh was served to Śakti, the son of his guru, who had requested a meal of meat. Discovering this, the enraged sage gave a curse to the king: 'You shall become a man-eater (a rākṣasa).' And the deluded king made a vow: 'I will devour you first along with your brothers!'
18. In the eighteenth chapter:

7.20.s: sabhāryasya saudāsasya vanapraveśaḥ . tatra rakṣobhāvamāpannena tena vasiṣṭhasya paśyataḥ sabhrātṛśatasya śakterbhakṣaṇam . putraśokānunaptasya vasiṣṭhapyātmahatyārthaṃ prayatnaḥ . (śatadru) vipāśādi - nāma - niruktiḥ . vasiṣṭhena rājño rakṣobhāvāt mocanam . rājñaḥkṣetre putrotpādanam . adṛśyantyā garbhataḥ parāśarasyotpattiḥ . parāśarakṛto rakṣaḥ- satrasamārambhaḥ .
7.20.d: सभार्यस्य सौदासस्य वनप्रवेशः . तत्र रक्षोभावमापन्नेन तेन वसिष्ठस्य पश्यतः सभ्रातृशतस्य शक्तेर्भक्षणम् . पुत्रशोकानुनप्तस्य वसिष्ठप्यात्महत्यार्थं प्रयत्नः . (शतद्रु) विपाशादि - नाम - निरुक्तिः . वसिष्ठेन राज्ञो रक्षोभावात् मोचनम् . राज्ञःक्षेत्रे पुत्रोत्पादनम् . अदृश्यन्त्या गर्भतः पराशरस्योत्पत्तिः . पराशरकृतो रक्षः- सत्रसमारम्भः .
7.20.m: The entry into the forest by Saudāsa together with his wife. There, having assumed the state of a demon, he devours Śakti along with his hundred brothers before the eyes of Vasiṣṭha. The attempt at suicide by Vasiṣṭha, tormented by grief for his sons. The etymological derivation of the names Śatadru, Vipāś, and others. The liberation of the king from the state of a demon by Vasiṣṭha. The procreation of a son upon the king's field [his wife]. The birth of Parāśara from the womb of Adṛśyantī. The commencement of the demon-sacrifice performed by Parāśara.
19. In the nineteenth chapter:

7.20.s: vasipṭhānurodhāt parāśarasyāpatyārthaṃ maināke tapaścaraṇam . parāśarāt kālyāṃ vyāsasyotpattiḥ . vyāsāt śukotpattiḥ, śukasya putracatuṣṭaya kanyā caiketyanvayoddeśaḥ, . putraśataghātānantaramapyapraśāntavaireṇa viśvāmitreṇa vasiṣṭhajighṛkṣayā sarasvatyāḥ sāhāyyābhyarthanā . sarasvatyāḥ srotovegena vasiṣṭhasyāśramādapavāhanam . viśvāmitra- śāpāt sarasvatyā asṛktoyatvam . viśvāmitrasya vasiṣṭhajighāṃsā . dvayoranyo'nyamugrasaṃmardaḥ . sarṣīṇāṃ devānāmabhyarthanayā dvayoḥ pravardhamānavairatyāgena parasparaṃ sakhyāṅgīkāraḥ . sarasvatyāḥ svacchajalatvam .
7.20.d: वसिप्ठानुरोधात् पराशरस्यापत्यार्थं मैनाके तपश्चरणम् . पराशरात् काल्यां व्यासस्योत्पत्तिः . व्यासात् शुकोत्पत्तिः, शुकस्य पुत्रचतुष्टय कन्या चैकेत्यन्वयोद्देशः, . पुत्रशतघातानन्तरमप्यप्रशान्तवैरेण विश्वामित्रेण वसिष्ठजिघृक्षया सरस्वत्याः साहाय्याभ्यर्थना . सरस्वत्याः स्रोतोवेगेन वसिष्ठस्याश्रमादपवाहनम् . विश्वामित्र- शापात् सरस्वत्या असृक्तोयत्वम् . विश्वामित्रस्य वसिष्ठजिघांसा . द्वयोरन्योऽन्यमुग्रसंमर्दः . सर्षीणां देवानामभ्यर्थनया द्वयोः प्रवर्धमानवैरत्यागेन परस्परं सख्याङ्गीकारः . सरस्वत्याः स्वच्छजलत्वम् .
7.20.m: The performance of austerity by Parāśara on Mount Maināka for the sake of offspring at the behest of Vasiṣṭha. The birth of Vyāsa from Parāśara upon Kālī. The birth of Śuka from Vyāsa; an account of Śuka's lineage as four sons and one daughter. The request for assistance from Sarasvatī by Viśvāmitra desiring to seize Vasiṣṭha, his enmity remaining unabated even after the slaughter of the hundred sons. The carrying away of Vasiṣṭha from his hermitage by the force of Sarasvatī's current. The turning of Sarasvatī's water into blood due to Viśvāmitra's curse. Viśvāmitra's desire to slay Vasiṣṭha. A fierce clash between the two. The mutual acceptance of friendship through the abandonment of their growing enmity at the entreaty of the gods along with the seers. Sarasvatī's waters becoming clear again.
20. In the twentieth chapter:

7.20.s: nandyupākhyānārambhaḥ, śilādasya putrārthaṃ tapaścaryā . śilādakṛtā devadevastutiḥ, varalābhaḥ, nandina utpattiḥ . mahādevadarśanena tadanugrahalipsayā nandino gṛhānnirgamanam .
7.20.d: नन्द्युपाख्यानारम्भः, शिलादस्य पुत्रार्थं तपश्चर्या . शिलादकृता देवदेवस्तुतिः, वरलाभः, नन्दिन उत्पत्तिः . महादेवदर्शनेन तदनुग्रहलिप्सया नन्दिनो गृहान्निर्गमनम् .
7.20.m: The beginning of the narrative of Nandin; the performance of austerity by Śilāda for the sake of a son. The praise of the God of gods performed by Śilāda; the attainment of a boon; the birth of Nandin. The departure of Nandin from home, desiring His grace through the darśana of Mahādeva.
21. In the twenty-first chapter:

7.20.s: bhuvanāṃ praviśya tadantarjale nandino'nekakoṭirūdrajāpaḥ . devadevadarśanam . nandikṛtā devadevastutiḥ .
7.20.d: भुवनां प्रविश्य तदन्तर्जले नन्दिनोऽनेककोटिरूद्रजापः . देवदेवदर्शनम् . नन्दिकृता देवदेवस्तुतिः .
7.20.m: Nandin, having entered Bhuvanā, recites the Rudra-mantra many millions of times within its water. The darśana of the God of gods. The hymn of praise to the God of gods performed by Nandin.
22. In the twenty-second chapter:
The grace of the God of gods towards Nandin. The origin of Japyeśvara. The narrative of Pañcanada.
23. In the twenty-third chapter:

7.20.s: nandinaḥ senāpatyābhiṣekopakramaḥ. tadarthaṃ gaṇānāmāhvānam . akhilagaṇapasamājopasthitiḥ . teṣāmaśeṣato nāmārūpa- saṃkhyādivivaraṇam .
7.20.d: नन्दिनः सेनापत्याभिषेकोपक्रमः. तदर्थं गणानामाह्वानम् . अखिलगणपसमाजोपस्थितिः . तेषामशेषतो नामारूप- संख्यादिविवरणम् .
7.20.m: The commencement of the consecration of Nandin as commander-in-chief. The summoning of the hosts for that purpose. The arrival of the entire assembly of host-leaders. The detailed description of their names, forms, numbers, and the like, without remainder.
24. In the twenty-fourth chapter:

7.20.s: devadevājñayā gaṇapānāṃ sarvasaṃbhāropasthāpanam . sarvadevānāṃ sarṣīṇāṃ tatrāgamaḥ . devadevyoḥ samakṣaṃ paryāyeṇa brahmādikṛto maharddhiyukto nandinaḥ senāpatyebhiṣekaḥ . brahmādikṛtā nandistutiḥ . sarvato jayakāraśca .
7.20.d: देवदेवाज्ञया गणपानां सर्वसंभारोपस्थापनम् . सर्वदेवानां सर्षीणां तत्रागमः . देवदेव्योः समक्षं पर्यायेण ब्रह्मादिकृतो महर्द्धियुक्तो नन्दिनः सेनापत्येभिषेकः . ब्रह्मादिकृता नन्दिस्तुतिः . सर्वतो जयकारश्च .
7.20.m: The bringing forth of all the provisions by the host-leaders at the command of the God of gods. The arrival there of all the gods along with the seers. The consecration of Nandin as commander-in-chief, accompanied by great splendor, performed in turn by Brahmā and the others in the presence of the God and the Goddess. The praise of Nandin performed by Brahmā and the others; and shouts of victory on all sides.
25. In the twenty-fifth chapter:

7.20.s: nandina kṛte mahādevena tatra marutāṃ sakāśe kanyāyācanam . marutkanyayā suyaśayā saha nandino vivāhaḥ . nikhilairgaṇairnandino'bhinandanama . nandikṛtā gaṇānāṃ stutiḥ .
7.20.d: नन्दिन कृते महादेवेन तत्र मरुतां सकाशे कन्यायाचनम् . मरुत्कन्यया सुयशया सह नन्दिनो विवाहः . निखिलैर्गणैर्नन्दिनोऽभिनन्दनम . नन्दिकृता गणानां स्तुतिः .
7.20.m: The request for a maiden from the Maruts there by Mahādeva on behalf of Nandin. The marriage of Nandin with Suyaśā, the daughter of the Maruts. The congratulation of Nandin by all the hosts. The praise of the hosts performed by Nandin.
26. In the twenty-sixth chapter:

7.20.s: ekadā svecchayā pārvatyā mātṛgṛhagamanam . tatra māturmukhād bhartṛviṣayakāsaṃbhāvitāsaṃmatahīnavacanaśravaṇam . tato nātihṛṣṭamanasā nivṛtya bhartuḥ pārśve samāgatayā tayā parvataṃ vihāya nivāsārthaṃ sthalāntaragamanecchāprakaṭanam . tadarthaṃ śivena nikumbhanāmānaṃ gaṇeśvaramāhūya tasya divodāsādhyuṣitāyā vārāṇāsyāḥ śūnyīkaraṇārthamājñādānam . tadanusāraṃ nikumbhasya vārāṇāsīṃ gatvā nāpitasāhāyyena mandiraṃ nirmāya tatra nijapratimāyāḥ pratiṣṭhāpanam . tataśca tatra varadagaṇeśarūpeṇa nikumbhasyāvasthānam . svāvahelanaṃ vyājīkṛtya tena samahiṣīkasya divodāsasya tataḥ utsādanam . evaṃ śūnyīkṛtāyāṃ vārāṇasyāmāgatya somasya sagaṇasya devadevasya nivasanam .
7.20.d: एकदा स्वेच्छया पार्वत्या मातृगृहगमनम् . तत्र मातुर्मुखाद् भर्तृविषयकासंभावितासंमतहीनवचनश्रवणम् . ततो नातिहृष्टमनसा निवृत्य भर्तुः पार्श्वे समागतया तया पर्वतं विहाय निवासार्थं स्थलान्तरगमनेच्छाप्रकटनम् . तदर्थं शिवेन निकुम्भनामानं गणेश्वरमाहूय तस्य दिवोदासाध्युषिताया वाराणास्याः शून्यीकरणार्थमाज्ञादानम् . तदनुसारं निकुम्भस्य वाराणासीं गत्वा नापितसाहाय्येन मन्दिरं निर्माय तत्र निजप्रतिमायाः प्रतिष्ठापनम् . ततश्च तत्र वरदगणेशरूपेण निकुम्भस्यावस्थानम् . स्वावहेलनं व्याजीकृत्य तेन समहिषीकस्य दिवोदासस्य ततः उत्सादनम् . एवं शून्यीकृतायां वाराणस्यामागत्य सोमस्य सगणस्य देवदेवस्य निवसनम् .
7.20.m: Once Pārvatī goes of her own accord to her mother's house. There, from her mother's mouth, she hears impossible, disagreeable, and disparaging words concerning her husband. Then, returning to her husband's presence with a mind not very pleased, she reveals her desire to go to another place to reside, having abandoned the mountain. For that purpose, Śiva summons the host-lord named Nikumbha and issues an order to depopulate Vārāṇasī, which was inhabited by Divodāsa. In accordance with that, Nikumbha goes to Vārāṇasī, builds a temple with the help of a barber, and installs his own image there. Then Nikumbha remains there in the form of Gaṇeśa the granter of boons. Making an insult to himself a pretext, he drives Divodāsa along with his queen out of that place. Thus, the God of gods, accompanied by the Moon and attended by His hosts, comes and resides in the vacated Vārāṇasī.
27. In the twenty-seventh chapter:

7.20.s: pārvatyā pṛṣṭena śambhunā bhaktānugrahārthaṃ svaprāsādanirmāṇa saṃmārjanopalepana śubhrīkaraṇa liṅgasthāpanapūjanasnapanā- bhigamanānuyānavividhadravyadānopacārasamarpaṇādiphalakathanam .
7.20.d: पार्वत्या पृष्टेन शम्भुना भक्तानुग्रहार्थं स्वप्रासादनिर्माण संमार्जनोपलेपन शुभ्रीकरण लिङ्गस्थापनपूजनस्नपना- भिगमनानुयानविविधद्रव्यदानोपचारसमर्पणादिफलकथनम् .
7.20.m: Questioned by Pārvatī, Śambhu relates the fruits of building, sweeping, smearing, and whitewashing His temple, installing, worshipping, bathing with a ceremonial bath, approaching, and following the liṅga, and offering various materials and services, for the sake of bestowing grace upon devotees.
28. In the twenty-eighth chapter:
The narration of the fruits of various vows, fasts, austerities, observances, gifts, recitations, and chanting of names dedicated to Śambhu and pleasing to Him.
29. In the twenty-ninth chapter:

7.20.s: somasya devadevasya vārāṇasīkṣetre svakṛtadivyodyānadarśanam . śambhukṛtaṃ goprekṣeśvarakapilāhradabhadradohopaśāntaśiva- hiraṇyagarbheśvara svalīneśvaravyāghreśvara jyeṣṭhasthānāvimuktaśaileśvarasaṃgameśvaramadhyameśvaraśukreśvarajambukeśvarāvimukteśvara- vārāṇasījāhnavyādīnāṃ puṇyakṣetrāṇāṃ nāmanirvacanapūrvaka māhātmyakathanam . tadaiva pārvatyā pāśupatavratināṃ yogināṃ jyotirmaye ṣaḍviṃśe parasmin puruṣe layadarśanam . evaṃ svapuṇyasthānānyākhyāya śambhunā punaravimuktakṣetrasya (kāśyā) bhāgīrathyāśca vistareṇa māhātmyakathanam .
7.20.d: सोमस्य देवदेवस्य वाराणसीक्षेत्रे स्वकृतदिव्योद्यानदर्शनम् . शम्भुकृतं गोप्रेक्षेश्वरकपिलाह्रदभद्रदोहोपशान्तशिव- हिरण्यगर्भेश्वर स्वलीनेश्वरव्याघ्रेश्वर ज्येष्ठस्थानाविमुक्तशैलेश्वरसंगमेश्वरमध्यमेश्वरशुक्रेश्वरजम्बुकेश्वराविमुक्तेश्वर- वाराणसीजाह्नव्यादीनां पुण्यक्षेत्राणां नामनिर्वचनपूर्वक माहात्म्यकथनम् . तदैव पार्वत्या पाशुपतव्रतिनां योगिनां ज्योतिर्मये षड्विंशे परस्मिन् पुरुषे लयदर्शनम् . एवं स्वपुण्यस्थानान्याख्याय शम्भुना पुनरविमुक्तक्षेत्रस्य (काश्या) भागीरथ्याश्च विस्तरेण माहात्म्यकथनम् .
7.20.m: The God of gods, accompanied by the Moon, beholds the divine garden created by Himself in the sacred field of Vārāṇasī. The narration by Śambhu, accompanied by etymological explanations of the names, of the māhātmya of the sacred fields such as Goprekṣeśvara, Kapilāhrada, Bhadradoha, Upaśāntaśiva, Hiraṇyagarbheśvara, Svalīneśvara, Vyāghreśvara, the Jyeṣṭhasthāna, Avimukta, Śaileśvara, Saṅgameśvara, Madhyameśvara, Śukreśvara, Jambukeśvara, Avimukteśvara, Vārāṇasī, and Jāhnavī. At that very time, Pārvatī beholds the dissolution of the yogins observing the Pāśupata vow into the twenty-sixth Supreme Person consisting of light. Having thus spoken of His sacred places, Śambhu again narrates in detail the māhātmya of the Avimukta sacred field (Kāśī) and of the Bhāgīrathī.
30. In the thirtieth chapter:

7.20.s: jaigīṣavyatapaścaryā, jaigīṣavyaṃ prati śivasyānugrahaḥ . jaigīṣavyakṛtā śivastutiḥ, varalābhaḥ . kuberatapaścaryā, tatsannidhau śivayorāgamanam, kubereṇa kaṭākṣadṛṣṭyā 'nimiṣeṇa pārvartāmukhanirīkṣaṇam . pārvatyāḥ kopaḥ . kuberasya piṅgākṣatvam, kuberakṛtā devadevastutiḥ . kuberaṃ prati śivasyānugrahaḥ . paṃcacūḍānāṃ tapaścaryā, śivayostāsāṃ darśanadā- nam . paṃcacūḍābhiḥ kṛtā pārvatīstutiḥ . tābhyaḥ pārvatyā varapradānam .
7.20.d: जैगीषव्यतपश्चर्या, जैगीषव्यं प्रति शिवस्यानुग्रहः . जैगीषव्यकृता शिवस्तुतिः, वरलाभः . कुबेरतपश्चर्या, तत्सन्निधौ शिवयोरागमनम्, कुबेरेण कटाक्षदृष्ट्या ऽनिमिषेण पार्वर्तामुखनिरीक्षणम् . पार्वत्याः कोपः . कुबेरस्य पिङ्गाक्षत्वम्, कुबेरकृता देवदेवस्तुतिः . कुबेरं प्रति शिवस्यानुग्रहः . पंचचूडानां तपश्चर्या, शिवयोस्तासां दर्शनदा- नम् . पंचचूडाभिः कृता पार्वतीस्तुतिः . ताभ्यः पार्वत्या वरप्रदानम् .
7.20.m: The performance of austerity by Jaigīṣavya; Śiva's grace toward Jaigīṣavya. The praise of Śiva performed by Jaigīṣavya; the attainment of a boon. The performance of austerity by Kubera; the arrival of Śiva and Pārvatī into his presence; Kubera gazing unblinkingly with a side-glance upon Pārvatī's face. The anger of Pārvatī. Kubera's eyes becoming yellowish-brown; the praise of the God of gods performed by Kubera. Śiva's grace toward Kubera. The performance of austerity by the Pañcacūḍās; the bestowing of darśana upon them by Śiva and Pārvatī. The praise of Pārvatī performed by the Pañcacūḍās. The granting of a boon to them by Pārvatī.
31. In the thirty-first chapter:

7.20.s: harikeśāparanāmnaḥ piṅgalayakṣasya śivaparāyaṇasya gaṇatvaprāptiḥ . pārvatyāḥ punarudyānadidṛkṣā . kāśīkṣetra- māhātmyaśravaṇecchā ca . śambhunā pārvatyā udyānadarśanam . vistareṇodyānavarṇanam . avimuktāparanāmnaḥ kāśīkṣetrasya māhātmyavarṇanam . jaigīṣavyaguhāyā ullekhaḥ . piṅgalāya varadānam, mandaratapaścaryā . sagaṇasya somasya śambhostapasyantaṃ mandaraṃ prati gamanam . tasmin śambhoranugraho varadānañca . prāgyajñamūrtijaladavāhanasya rudrasya paścād vṛṣavāhanatve kāraṇamākhyātuṃ purātanakathāvatāraṇam . kṣuvato brahmaṇo vaktrāt kṣupasyotpattiḥ . kṣupadadhīcivivādaḥ . viṣṇudadhīciyuddham, sthāneśvarasthāṇutīrthasthāṇuvaṭādimāhātmyavarṇanam .
7.20.d: हरिकेशापरनाम्नः पिङ्गलयक्षस्य शिवपरायणस्य गणत्वप्राप्तिः . पार्वत्याः पुनरुद्यानदिदृक्षा . काशीक्षेत्र- माहात्म्यश्रवणेच्छा च . शम्भुना पार्वत्या उद्यानदर्शनम् . विस्तरेणोद्यानवर्णनम् . अविमुक्तापरनाम्नः काशीक्षेत्रस्य माहात्म्यवर्णनम् . जैगीषव्यगुहाया उल्लेखः . पिङ्गलाय वरदानम्, मन्दरतपश्चर्या . सगणस्य सोमस्य शम्भोस्तपस्यन्तं मन्दरं प्रति गमनम् . तस्मिन् शम्भोरनुग्रहो वरदानञ्च . प्राग्यज्ञमूर्तिजलदवाहनस्य रुद्रस्य पश्चाद् वृषवाहनत्वे कारणमाख्यातुं पुरातनकथावतारणम् . क्षुवतो ब्रह्मणो वक्त्रात् क्षुपस्योत्पत्तिः . क्षुपदधीचिविवादः . विष्णुदधीचियुद्धम्, स्थानेश्वरस्थाणुतीर्थस्थाणुवटादिमाहात्म्यवर्णनम् .
7.20.m: Attainment of gaṇahood by the yakṣa Piṅgala, also named Harikeśa, who was devoted to Śiva. Pārvatī’s desire to see the garden again, and her wish to hear the māhātmya of the Kāśī kṣetra. Śambhu’s viewing of the garden with Pārvatī. Detailed description of the garden. Description of the māhātmya of the Kāśī kṣetra, which is also named Avimukta. Mention of the cave of Jaigīṣavya. Granting of a boon to Piṅgala; the tapas of Mandara. The arrival of Śambhu along with Soma and his gaṇas before the ascetic Mandara. Śambhu’s grace upon him and granting of a boon. Introduction of an ancient story to explain the reason why Rudra, who formerly rode upon the cloud-embodiment of sacrifice, subsequently took the bull as his mount. The birth of Kṣupa from the mouth of sneezing Brahmā. The dispute between Kṣupa and Dadhīci. The battle between Viṣṇu and Dadhīci; description of the māhātmya of Sthāneśvara, Sthāṇutīrtha, Sthāṇuvaṭa, and other places.
32. In the thirty-second chapter:

7.20.s: dakṣakṛtaḥ kratvanuṣṭhānārambhaḥ . tatra rudrāya yajñabhāgāpradānam. parvatīprakopaḥ . bhadrakālīharibhadra( vīrabhadra) - yorutpattiḥ . tatkṛtaṃ kratuvidhvaṃsanam . mṛgarūpeṇa palāyamānasya yajñasya vīrabhadrakṛtaḥ śīrṣacchedaḥ, devaiḥ kṛtā devadevastutiḥ . devānāṃ maheśvarodarapraviṣṭānāṃ vividhādbhutalokavicitrapuradarśanam . kālakarṇyā utpattiḥ tadbhayād devānāṃ bhasmakūṭe nilayanam . bhasmasaṃsargāt teṣāṃ pāśupatatvaprāptiḥ, devaiḥ kṛtā kālakarṇīstutiḥ, devānprati devadevasyānugrahaḥ . yajñasya mṛgaśīrṣatāsamāpattiḥ, bhadrakarṇahradabhadreśvarayormahimā haribhadrasya puṇyakṣetratvam, kubjāmrakabrahmāvarttayoḥ samākhyā . dakṣakṛtā pārvatīparameśvarayoḥ stutiḥ, dakṣaṃ prati śivayoranugrahaḥ . arjunānadī- kanakhalayornāmanirvacanaṃ samāhātmyam .
7.20.d: दक्षकृतः क्रत्वनुष्ठानारम्भः . तत्र रुद्राय यज्ञभागाप्रदानम्. पर्वतीप्रकोपः . भद्रकालीहरिभद्र( वीरभद्र) - योरुत्पत्तिः . तत्कृतं क्रतुविध्वंसनम् . मृगरूपेण पलायमानस्य यज्ञस्य वीरभद्रकृतः शीर्षच्छेदः, देवैः कृता देवदेवस्तुतिः . देवानां महेश्वरोदरप्रविष्टानां विविधाद्भुतलोकविचित्रपुरदर्शनम् . कालकर्ण्या उत्पत्तिः तद्भयाद् देवानां भस्मकूटे निलयनम् . भस्मसंसर्गात् तेषां पाशुपतत्वप्राप्तिः, देवैः कृता कालकर्णीस्तुतिः, देवान्प्रति देवदेवस्यानुग्रहः . यज्ञस्य मृगशीर्षतासमापत्तिः, भद्रकर्णह्रदभद्रेश्वरयोर्महिमा हरिभद्रस्य पुण्यक्षेत्रत्वम्, कुब्जाम्रकब्रह्मावर्त्तयोः समाख्या . दक्षकृता पार्वतीपरमेश्वरयोः स्तुतिः, दक्षं प्रति शिवयोरनुग्रहः . अर्जुनानदी- कनखलयोर्नामनिर्वचनं समाहात्म्यम् .
7.20.m: The commencement of the performance of the sacrificial rite undertaken by Dakṣa. The failure to offer a sacrificial share to Rudra therein. The anger of Pārvatī. The birth of Bhadrakālī and Haribhadra (Vīrabhadra). The destruction of the sacrificial rite wrought by them. The decapitation by Vīrabhadra of the sacrificial rite fleeing in the form of a deer; the praise of the God of Gods uttered by the gods. The sight of various wondrous worlds and extraordinary cities by the gods who had entered the belly of Maheśvara. The birth of Kālakarṇī; the hiding of the gods in a heap of ashes out of fear of her. Their attainment of the state of Pāśupatas through contact with the ashes; the praise of Kālakarṇī uttered by the gods; the grace of the God of Gods toward the gods. The assumption of the head of a deer by the sacrificial rite; the glory of the lake Bhadrakarṇahrada and Bhadreśvara; Haribhadra's status as a sacred kṣetra; the designation of Kubjāmraka and Brahmāvarta. The praise of Pārvatī and Parameśvara offered by Dakṣa; the grace of Śiva and Pārvatī toward Dakṣa. The etymology of the names of the river Arjunā and Kanakhala, along with their māhātmya.
33. In the thirty-third chapter:

7.20.s: rudravāhanatvakāmanayā dharmayajñayostapaścaryā, rudradarśanam. dharmayajñakṛtā rudrastutiḥ . janmāntarepi rudravāhanatvaprāptaye tayorabhyarthanā, yatheṣṭavarāvāptiḥ . atulaputraprāptyarthaṃ surabhyāstapaścaryā . surabhyā vṛṣabhotpattiḥ, ekādaśarūdrāṇā- mutpattiḥ, gokanyotpattiḥ (saptagavotpattiḥ) . vṛṣabhacaritākhyānam, caritatṛṇasya tṛṣārtasya vṛṣabhasya samudre jalapānārambhaḥ, samudraśoṣaṇāśaṅkayā vaḍavānalakṛto vṛṣabhanigrahaḥ . pītasya jalasyāśeṣataścharddanam, tathāvamānitasya vṛṣabhasya rudrārādhanam . tuṣṭasya rudrasya vṛṣabhaprārthanayā vaḍavānalanigrahaḥ paścāttadvisarjanaṃ ca . devatānāṃ prārthanayā rudreṇa vṛṣabhasya lokodvejakaraveganivāraṇāya prabhākaranāmno gaṇasya sarjanam . rudrasya vṛṣavāhanatvam, vṛṣabhasya sarvadevamayatvam, tadaṅgāvayaveṣu sarvabhūtasthitikathanam .
7.20.d: रुद्रवाहनत्वकामनया धर्मयज्ञयोस्तपश्चर्या, रुद्रदर्शनम्. धर्मयज्ञकृता रुद्रस्तुतिः . जन्मान्तरेपि रुद्रवाहनत्वप्राप्तये तयोरभ्यर्थना, यथेष्टवरावाप्तिः . अतुलपुत्रप्राप्त्यर्थं सुरभ्यास्तपश्चर्या . सुरभ्या वृषभोत्पत्तिः, एकादशरूद्राणा- मुत्पत्तिः, गोकन्योत्पत्तिः (सप्तगवोत्पत्तिः) . वृषभचरिताख्यानम्, चरिततृणस्य तृषार्तस्य वृषभस्य समुद्रे जलपानारम्भः, समुद्रशोषणाशङ्कया वडवानलकृतो वृषभनिग्रहः . पीतस्य जलस्याशेषतश्छर्द्दनम्, तथावमानितस्य वृषभस्य रुद्राराधनम् . तुष्टस्य रुद्रस्य वृषभप्रार्थनया वडवानलनिग्रहः पश्चात्तद्विसर्जनं च . देवतानां प्रार्थनया रुद्रेण वृषभस्य लोकोद्वेजकरवेगनिवारणाय प्रभाकरनाम्नो गणस्य सर्जनम् . रुद्रस्य वृषवाहनत्वम्, वृषभस्य सर्वदेवमयत्वम्, तदङ्गावयवेषु सर्वभूतस्थितिकथनम् .
7.20.m: The practice of tapas by Dharma and Yajña wishing to become Rudra’s mount; the vision of Rudra. The praise of Rudra offered by Dharma and Yajña. Their supplication to attain the status of Rudra’s mount even in another birth, and the attainment of the desired boon. Surabhi’s practice of tapas to obtain an peerless son. The birth of the bull from Surabhi; the birth of the eleven Rudras; the birth of the cow-maidens (the birth of the seven cows). The narration of the deeds of the bull; the thirsty bull, having grazed on grass, beginning to drink water in the ocean; the subjugation of the bull by the submarine fire fearing the drying up of the ocean. The vomiting up of the drunk water without remainder; the worship of Rudra by the bull thus humiliated. The subjugation of the submarine fire by the pleased Rudra at the bull’s prayer, and its subsequent release. The creation by Rudra, at the prayer of the deities, of the gaṇa named Prabhākara to restrain the bull’s velocity that distressed the worlds. Rudra’s taking the bull as his mount; the bull’s embodiment of all the gods; the account of the presence of all beings in the parts of his body.
34. In the thirty-fourth chapter:

7.20.s: devadevasya vṛṣavāhatvakathopasaṃhāraḥ . mahādevena kathāntare kṛṣṇetyuktāyāḥ pārvatyā gauravarṇatvaprāptaye putrasaṃjananārthaṃ ca himavacchikhare duścaratapaścaraṇam . pārvatyā alaṃkāratolaṃkāradhārākhyapuṇyasalilasaridutpattiḥ . pārvatyāṃ tapasi sthitāyāṃ tadbhakṣaṇoddeśena tatra samāgatasya śārdūlasya tatpratīkṣayā tasyāmanimeṣadṛṣṭestaddinātprabhṛti tatraiva niścalatayāvasthānam . upamanyūpākhyānam, upamanyoranāyāsopasthitakṣīrānnabhojanaprāptaye rudrārādhanam . yathepsita- varaprāptiḥ, upamanyukṛtā śivastutiḥ .
7.20.d: देवदेवस्य वृषवाहत्वकथोपसंहारः . महादेवेन कथान्तरे कृष्णेत्युक्तायाः पार्वत्या गौरवर्णत्वप्राप्तये पुत्रसंजननार्थं च हिमवच्छिखरे दुश्चरतपश्चरणम् . पार्वत्या अलंकारतोलंकारधाराख्यपुण्यसलिलसरिदुत्पत्तिः . पार्वत्यां तपसि स्थितायां तद्भक्षणोद्देशेन तत्र समागतस्य शार्दूलस्य तत्प्रतीक्षया तस्यामनिमेषदृष्टेस्तद्दिनात्प्रभृति तत्रैव निश्चलतयावस्थानम् . उपमन्यूपाख्यानम्, उपमन्योरनायासोपस्थितक्षीरान्नभोजनप्राप्तये रुद्राराधनम् . यथेप्सित- वरप्राप्तिः, उपमन्युकृता शिवस्तुतिः .
7.20.m: Conclusion of the story of the God of Gods taking the bull as his mount. The practice of severe tapas on the peak of Himavat by Pārvatī—who had been called ‘black’ by Mahādeva in another episode—in order to attain a fair complexion and to bring about the birth of a son. The emergence of the sacred river named Alaṅkāradhārā from Pārvatī’s ornaments. A tiger that arrived there with the intent to devour Pārvatī while she was engaged in tapas, remaining motionless right there from that day forward, waiting for her with unblinking gaze. The narrative of Upamanyu; Upamanyu’s worship of Rudra to obtain effortless meals of milk-rice. The attainment of the desired boon; the praise of Śiva uttered by Upamanyu.
35. In the thirty-fifth chapter:

7.20.s: sukeśopākhyānam,- sukeśasya pathi gacchato vane gartāntarvīraṇastambāśrita lambanānādhomukhasvapūrvajapitrādidarśanam . sukeśasya taduddharaṇopāyajijñāsā . sukeśāya pitṛkṛto'patyotpādanopadeśaḥ, ūrdhvaretasaḥ sataḥ sukeśasyāpatyo- tpādanamantareṇaiva pitṝṇāmuddhārārthaṃ rudrārādhanā, tuṣṭena rudreṇa sukeśapitṝṇāṃ narakāduddharaṇaṃ, tasya gāṇapatya- pradānaṃ ca .
7.20.d: सुकेशोपाख्यानम्,- सुकेशस्य पथि गच्छतो वने गर्तान्तर्वीरणस्तम्बाश्रित लम्बनानाधोमुखस्वपूर्वजपित्रादिदर्शनम् . सुकेशस्य तदुद्धरणोपायजिज्ञासा . सुकेशाय पितृकृतोऽपत्योत्पादनोपदेशः, ऊर्ध्वरेतसः सतः सुकेशस्यापत्यो- त्पादनमन्तरेणैव पितॄणामुद्धारार्थं रुद्राराधना, तुष्टेन रुद्रेण सुकेशपितॄणां नरकादुद्धरणं, तस्य गाणपत्य- प्रदानं च .
7.20.m: The narrative of Sukeśa: Sukeśa, traveling on a path in the forest, sees his ancestors—his father and others—hanging upside down suspended from a clump of vīraṇa grass inside a pit. Sukeśa’s inquiry into the means of their deliverance. The father’s instruction to Sukeśa to beget offspring; Sukeśa, being of chaste life (ūrdhvaretas), worships Rudra for the deliverance of his ancestors without begetting offspring; the deliverance of Sukeśa’s ancestors from hell by the pleased Rudra, and his bestowal of leadership of the gaṇas upon him.
36. In the thirty-sixth chapter:

7.20.s: sukeśatatpitṛsaṃvādaḥ, putrapraśaṃsā putrapadaniruktiśca . pitṛpadasamākhyānam . putrāṇāṃ pitṛtvaprāptyupākhyānam . nārakīyagatijijñāsayā pitṝnprati sukeśasya praśnaḥ .
7.20.d: सुकेशतत्पितृसंवादः, पुत्रप्रशंसा पुत्रपदनिरुक्तिश्च . पितृपदसमाख्यानम् . पुत्राणां पितृत्वप्राप्त्युपाख्यानम् . नारकीयगतिजिज्ञासया पितॄन्प्रति सुकेशस्य प्रश्नः .
7.20.m: Dialogue between Sukeśa and his ancestors; praise of the son and the etymological explanation of the word ‘putra’ (son). Explanation of the term ‘pitṛ’ (ancestor/father). The narrative of sons attaining the status of ancestors. Sukeśa’s question to the ancestors with the desire to know the fate of those in hell.
37. In the thirty-seventh chapter:

7.20.s: suśarmakṛtaṃ narakavarṇanam, yamalācalāditrayodaśanarakāṇāṃ nāmakathanam . taducchrayāṇāṃ sakhyopakathanam . pāpināṃ nākoyagatikramamaṃkṣepaḥ, sāmānyena narakayātanāvarṇanam . yamalācalanarakatadgāmijīvatatkarmatadyātanādīnāṃ varṇanam .
7.20.d: सुशर्मकृतं नरकवर्णनम्, यमलाचलादित्रयोदशनरकाणां नामकथनम् . तदुच्छ्रयाणां सख्योपकथनम् . पापिनां नाकोयगतिक्रममंक्षेपः, सामान्येन नरकयातनावर्णनम् . यमलाचलनरकतद्गामिजीवतत्कर्मतद्यातनादीनां वर्णनम् .
7.20.m: Description of the hells given by Suśarman; the enumeration of the names of the thirteen hells beginning with Yamalācala. Mention of the measurement of their heights. A summary of the course of the hellish fate of sinners; general description of the torments of hell. Description of the Yamalācala hell, the souls going thither, their actions, their torments, and so forth.
38. In the thirty-eighth chapter:
Description of the Kūṭaśālmali hell, the souls going thither, their actions, their torments, and so forth.
39. In the thirty-ninth chapter:
Description of the Kālasūtra hell, the souls going thither, their actions, their torments, and so forth.
40. In the fortieth chapter:
Description of the Kumbhīpāka hell, the souls going thither, their actions, their torments, and so forth.
41. In the forty-first chapter:
Description of the Asipatravana hell, the souls going thither, their actions, their torments, and so forth.
42. In the forty-second chapter:
Description of the river Vaitaraṇī, the souls falling into it, their actions, their torments, and so forth.
43. In the forty-third chapter:
Description of the Ayodhana hell, the souls going thither, their actions, their torments, and so forth.
44. In the forty-fourth chapter: / Description of the hell named Padma, the souls going thither, their actions, their torments, and so forth.
45. In the forty-fifth chapter:
Description of the hell named Mahāpadma, the souls going thither, their actions, their torments, and so forth.
46. In the forty-sixth chapter:
Description of the Raurava hell, the souls going thither, their actions, their torments, and so forth.
47. In the forty-seventh chapter:
Description of the Mahāraurava hell, the souls going thither, their actions, their torments, and so forth.
48. In the forty-eighth chapter:
Description of the hell named Tamas, the souls destined for it, their deeds, their torments, and so forth.
In the forty-ninth chapter:
Description of the hells Tamas and Tamatara, the souls destined for them, their deeds, their torments, and so forth.
In the fiftieth chapter:
Description of the order of obtaining various wombs, otherwise known as the cycle of transmigration, for the denizens of hell.
In the fifty-first chapter:

7.20.s: nārakīyāṇāṃ jīvānāmuddhārārthaṃ sukeśasya punarduścaratapaścaraṇena rudrārādhanam . rūdraprasādato'śeṣajīvānāṃ sadyo narakāduddhāraḥ .
7.20.d: नारकीयाणां जीवानामुद्धारार्थं सुकेशस्य पुनर्दुश्चरतपश्चरणेन रुद्राराधनम् . रूद्रप्रसादतोऽशेषजीवानां सद्यो नरकादुद्धारः .
7.20.m: Sukeśa's propitiation of Rudra through the practice of severe austerity once again for the purpose of redeeming the denizens of hell; the instantaneous deliverance of all living beings from hell by the grace of Rudra.
In the fifty-second chapter:

7.20.s: narakagatinivārakāṇāṃ śubhakarmaṇāṃ kathanam, sukeśopākhyānopasaṃhāraḥ . kāṣṭhakūṭopākhyānam, bhūmanyunāmno gautamakulotpannasyāputrasya vṛddhabrāhmaṇasya rudrārādhanataḥ, suyaśānāmnyā patnyāṃ kāṣṭhakūṭanāmasutotpattiḥ . kāṣṭha- kūṭasya vipravaṭoḥ pitroranumatyā vidyādhyayanārthaṃ gṛhānnirgatya cyavanasavidhe gamanam . tadantare bhūmanyordiṣṭāntaprāptiḥ, kāṣṭhakūṭe ' dhyayanaṃ samāpya gṛhaṃ pratyāgate bhartṛśokākulāyāstanmāturapi prāṇatyāgaḥ . kāṣṭhakūṭasya rudrārādhanam rudrānugraheṇa kāṣṭhakūṭasya gāṇapatyaprāptiḥ . tatpitrorujjīvanam, teṣāṃ śvetaparvate nivasanam, kāṣṭhakūṭopākhyānaupa- saṃhāraḥ . upamanyusukeśakāṣṭhakūṭādiṣu mahādevasya yosāvanugrahaḥ sa devyāṃ tapasi sthitāyāṃ saṃvṛtta iti kathanam .
7.20.d: नरकगतिनिवारकाणां शुभकर्मणां कथनम्, सुकेशोपाख्यानोपसंहारः . काष्ठकूटोपाख्यानम्, भूमन्युनाम्नो गौतमकुलोत्पन्नस्यापुत्रस्य वृद्धब्राह्मणस्य रुद्राराधनतः, सुयशानाम्न्या पत्न्यां काष्ठकूटनामसुतोत्पत्तिः . काष्ठ- कूटस्य विप्रवटोः पित्रोरनुमत्या विद्याध्ययनार्थं गृहान्निर्गत्य च्यवनसविधे गमनम् . तदन्तरे भूमन्योर्दिष्टान्तप्राप्तिः, काष्ठकूटे ' ध्ययनं समाप्य गृहं प्रत्यागते भर्तृशोकाकुलायास्तन्मातुरपि प्राणत्यागः . काष्ठकूटस्य रुद्राराधनम् रुद्रानुग्रहेण काष्ठकूटस्य गाणपत्यप्राप्तिः . तत्पित्रोरुज्जीवनम्, तेषां श्वेतपर्वते निवसनम्, काष्ठकूटोपाख्यानौप- संहारः . उपमन्युसुकेशकाष्ठकूटादिषु महादेवस्य योसावनुग्रहः स देव्यां तपसि स्थितायां संवृत्त इति कथनम् .
7.20.m: Account of auspicious deeds that avert going to hell; conclusion of the episode of Sukeśa. The episode of Kāṣṭhakūṭa: through propitiation of Rudra by an aged childless brahmin named Bhūmanyu, born of the Gautama family, the birth of a son named Kāṣṭhakūṭa to his wife named Suyaśā; departure of the young brahmin boy Kāṣṭhakūṭa from home with his parents' permission to study sacred lore in the presence of Cyavana; meanwhile, the death of Bhūmanyu; when Kāṣṭhakūṭa, having finished his studies, returned home, his mother also, overcome with grief for her husband, gave up her life; Kāṣṭhakūṭa's propitiation of Rudra; Kāṣṭhakūṭa's attainment of the status of a gaṇa-chief by Rudra's grace; the revival of his parents; their dwelling on the white mountain; conclusion of the episode of Kāṣṭhakūṭa. Statement that this grace shown by Mahādeva unto Upamanyu, Sukeśa, Kāṣṭhakūṭa, and others took place while the Goddess was engaged in austerity.
In the fifty-third chapter:

7.20.s: devyāstapaḥ prabhāveṇa lokānāṃ sthitiviparyayaṃ dṛṣṭavā bhītānāṃ brahmādīnāṃ śaṃkaradidṛkṣayā divyena vimānena mandārācalagamanam .
7.20.d: देव्यास्तपः प्रभावेण लोकानां स्थितिविपर्ययं दृष्टवा भीतानां ब्रह्मादीनां शंकरदिदृक्षया दिव्येन विमानेन मन्दाराचलगमनम् .
7.20.m: Seeing the overturning of the cosmic order caused by the power of the Goddess's austerity, Brahmā and the others, terrified, go by divine aerial chariot to Mount Mandara wishing to see Śaṃkara.
In the fifty-fourth chapter:

7.20.s: śivājñayā brahmādīnāṃ tataḥ parāvṛtya himavacchikhare tapaścarantyā devyāḥ samīpe gamanam .
7.20.d: शिवाज्ञया ब्रह्मादीनां ततः परावृत्य हिमवच्छिखरे तपश्चरन्त्या देव्याः समीपे गमनम् .
7.20.m: By Śiva's command, Brahmā and the others return from there and go before the Goddess, who was practicing austerity on a peak of the Himālaya.
In the fifty-fifth chapter:

7.20.s: brahmaṇo'bhyarthanayā pārvatyāstapaso vinivṛttiḥ . brahmaṇā vareṇacchandanam . pārvatyā prathamaṃ vyāghrasya kṛte varayācanam. brahmaṇā vyāghrasya somanandināmanirdeśanapuraḥsaraṃ gaṇatvapradānam . brahmaṇaḥ sakāśe pārvatyāḥ svasya gauravarṇatvāya lokottaramahimaputraprāptaye ca prārthanā . brahmaṇā pārvatyā yathābhilaṣitavarapradānam .
7.20.d: ब्रह्मणोऽभ्यर्थनया पार्वत्यास्तपसो विनिवृत्तिः . ब्रह्मणा वरेणच्छन्दनम् . पार्वत्या प्रथमं व्याघ्रस्य कृते वरयाचनम्. ब्रह्मणा व्याघ्रस्य सोमनन्दिनामनिर्देशनपुरःसरं गणत्वप्रदानम् . ब्रह्मणः सकाशे पार्वत्याः स्वस्य गौरवर्णत्वाय लोकोत्तरमहिमपुत्रप्राप्तये च प्रार्थना . ब्रह्मणा पार्वत्या यथाभिलषितवरप्रदानम् .
7.20.m: Cessation of Pārvatī's austerity upon Brahmā's supplication; enticement [of her] by Brahmā with a boon; Pārvatī's requesting a boon first on behalf of the tiger; Brahmā's conferring the status of a gaṇa [on the tiger] while bestowing the name Somanandin; Pārvatī's prayer before Brahmā for obtaining a fair complexion for herself and a son of extraordinary greatness; Brahmā's granting of the desired boon to Pārvatī.
In the fifty-sixth chapter:

7.20.s: duṣkṛtakarmaṇā durgatiṃ gatānāmapi pitṛbhaktivaśācchubhagatiprāpterudāharaṇāya somanandinaḥ pūrvavṛttamākhyātuṃ saptavyādhopākhyānam . saptānāṃ dvijaśiṣyāṇāṃ gurorvacanād gāmānetuṃ daśārṇato māhiṣmatīgamanam . gurvarthe gāmādāya pratinivartamānānāṃ teṣāṃ pathi durbhikṣavaśād nirāhāratayā mumūrṣūṇāṃ kṣudhāturāṇāṃ gatyantarābhāvāt- pitruddeśena tāmeva gāmālabhya tanmāṃsabhakṣaṇam . tadvijñāya kruddhena guruṇā teṣāṃ kaṣṭā gatirbhavitrīti śāpapradānam . guruśāpavaśānnaṣṭasaṃjñānāṃ teṣāṃ daśārṇātīravartini vane vyādhaputratvena janmagrahaṇam . vyādhavṛttyā vane vicaratāṃ teṣāṃ karuṇāviṣṭacetasopādhyāyena jātismaraṇayogyatāpādanenānugrahakaraṇam . tato gṛhaṃ pratyāgatānāṃ teṣāṃ tatpitrā vyādhena svapūrvavṛttakathanam . vyādhe pitari svaryāte mātari ca saṃsthitāyāṃ saptānāmapi teṣāṃ kālañjarādiṣu krameṇa mṛgādijanmaprāptiḥ . cakravākayonau vartamānānāṃ teṣāṃ saptānāṃ madhye prathameṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ kāmpilyādhipateraṇuhasya sāntaḥpurasya sarovare jalakrīḍādarśanājjātarāgāṇāṃ yathākramaṃ brahmadattabrahmadhanvapāñcālanāmnā rājapurohitamantri- putratvena janmagrahaṇam .
7.20.d: दुष्कृतकर्मणा दुर्गतिं गतानामपि पितृभक्तिवशाच्छुभगतिप्राप्तेरुदाहरणाय सोमनन्दिनः पूर्ववृत्तमाख्यातुं सप्तव्याधोपाख्यानम् . सप्तानां द्विजशिष्याणां गुरोर्वचनाद् गामानेतुं दशार्णतो माहिष्मतीगमनम् . गुर्वर्थे गामादाय प्रतिनिवर्तमानानां तेषां पथि दुर्भिक्षवशाद् निराहारतया मुमूर्षूणां क्षुधातुराणां गत्यन्तराभावात्- पित्रुद्देशेन तामेव गामालभ्य तन्मांसभक्षणम् . तद्विज्ञाय क्रुद्धेन गुरुणा तेषां कष्टा गतिर्भवित्रीति शापप्रदानम् . गुरुशापवशान्नष्टसंज्ञानां तेषां दशार्णातीरवर्तिनि वने व्याधपुत्रत्वेन जन्मग्रहणम् . व्याधवृत्त्या वने विचरतां तेषां करुणाविष्टचेतसोपाध्यायेन जातिस्मरणयोग्यतापादनेनानुग्रहकरणम् . ततो गृहं प्रत्यागतानां तेषां तत्पित्रा व्याधेन स्वपूर्ववृत्तकथनम् . व्याधे पितरि स्वर्याते मातरि च संस्थितायां सप्तानामपि तेषां कालञ्जरादिषु क्रमेण मृगादिजन्मप्राप्तिः . चक्रवाकयोनौ वर्तमानानां तेषां सप्तानां मध्ये प्रथमेषां त्रयाणां काम्पिल्याधिपतेरणुहस्य सान्तःपुरस्य सरोवरे जलक्रीडादर्शनाज्जातरागाणां यथाक्रमं ब्रह्मदत्तब्रह्मधन्वपाञ्चालनाम्ना राजपुरोहितमन्त्रि- पुत्रत्वेन जन्मग्रहणम् .
7.20.m: The tale of the seven hunters to narrate the past life of Somanandin, as an illustration of how even those who fall into an evil realm of existence on account of sinful deeds attain an auspicious realm through devotion to parents: the going of seven brahmin disciples from Daśārṇa to Māhiṣmatī to fetch a cow at the bidding of their guru; as they return with the cow for the guru's sake, being without food on the road due to famine, starving, on the verge of death, and having no other recourse, their slaughtering of that very cow dedicated to the ancestors and eating its flesh; the guru, upon learning this, angrily uttering a curse that they shall have a dreadful fate; losing their consciousness on account of the guru's curse, their taking birth as sons of a hunter in a forest on the banks of the Daśārṇā; as they wander in the forest living as hunters, the teacher, his heart filled with compassion, confers grace upon them by granting them the ability to remember their past births; then, after they return home, the narration of their past deeds by their father, the hunter; when their hunter father departed to heaven and their mother died, all seven sequentially obtain births as deer and so on on Kālañjara and elsewhere; among the seven living in the form of cakravāka birds, the first three, smitten with passion upon seeing the water sports of Aṇuha, the king of Kāmpilya, with his harem in a lake, take birth respectively as the sons of the king, the royal priest, and the minister under the names Brahmadatta, Brahmadhanvan, and Pāñcāla.
In the fifty-seventh chapter:

7.20.s: anyeṣāṃ caturṇāṃ cakravākānāṃ tatraiva kasyacidyāyāvarasya sutatvena janmagrahaṇam . brahmadattasya pañcālabrahmadhanvabhyāṃ saha bahukālaṃ kāmpilye rājyasukhabhogaḥ . tadanantaraṃ caturṇāṃ yāyāvarasutānāṃ yogeśvarāṇāṃ saṃketaślokadvayaśravaṇena jātasmṛterbrahmadattasya vane gatvā yogena tanutyāgaḥ . pañcālasya tapasā yakṣatvaprāptiḥ . brahmadhanvanaśca devadevyā ārādhanataḥ kāmarūpitvaprāptiḥ . hālopākhyānam, bhalandanopākhyānam . kāmavaśād vyāghrarūpeṇa ṛṣiṃ saṃtrāsya riraṃsayā ṛṣipatnīṃ dharṣayato brahmadhanvanastasyāḥ śāpavaśād vyāghrayoniṃ prāptiriti somanandinaḥ pūrvavṛttopasaṃhāraḥ . 58 aṣṭapaṃcāśattamedhyāye - brahmaṇo varalābhādanantaraṃ kṛṣṇavarṇāpahānāya pārvatyāḥ sarasi snānam . sarasi snātāyāḥ pārvatyāḥ śarīrakośataḥ kauśikyutpattiḥ . devyājñayā kauśikyā durgānāmnā vindhyaśikhare nivasanam .
7.20.d: अन्येषां चतुर्णां चक्रवाकानां तत्रैव कस्यचिद्यायावरस्य सुतत्वेन जन्मग्रहणम् . ब्रह्मदत्तस्य पञ्चालब्रह्मधन्वभ्यां सह बहुकालं काम्पिल्ये राज्यसुखभोगः . तदनन्तरं चतुर्णां यायावरसुतानां योगेश्वराणां संकेतश्लोकद्वयश्रवणेन जातस्मृतेर्ब्रह्मदत्तस्य वने गत्वा योगेन तनुत्यागः . पञ्चालस्य तपसा यक्षत्वप्राप्तिः . ब्रह्मधन्वनश्च देवदेव्या आराधनतः कामरूपित्वप्राप्तिः . हालोपाख्यानम्, भलन्दनोपाख्यानम् . कामवशाद् व्याघ्ररूपेण ऋषिं संत्रास्य रिरंसया ऋषिपत्नीं धर्षयतो ब्रह्मधन्वनस्तस्याः शापवशाद् व्याघ्रयोनिं प्राप्तिरिति सोमनन्दिनः पूर्ववृत्तोपसंहारः . 58 अष्टपंचाशत्तमेध्याये - ब्रह्मणो वरलाभादनन्तरं कृष्णवर्णापहानाय पार्वत्याः सरसि स्नानम् . सरसि स्नातायाः पार्वत्याः शरीरकोशतः कौशिक्युत्पत्तिः . देव्याज्ञया कौशिक्या दुर्गानाम्ना विन्ध्यशिखरे निवसनम् .
7.20.m: The other four cakravākas taking birth in that very place as the sons of a wandering ascetic; Brahmadatta enjoying royal pleasures for a long time in Kāmpilya together with Pāñcāla and Brahmadhanvan; thereafter, upon hearing two cryptic verses from the four sons of the wandering ascetic who were masters of yoga, Brahmadatta, having regained memory [of his past lives], goes to the forest and casts off his body through yoga; Pāñcāla attains the status of a yakṣa through austerity; Brahmadhanvan attains the power of assuming forms at will through propitiation of the God and Goddess; the episode of Hāla, the episode of Bhalandana; Brahmadhanvan, overcome by passion, having frightened a seer in the form of a tiger and seeking to violate the seer's wife out of lust, obtains birth as a tiger on account of her curse—thus the conclusion of the past history of Somanandin. In the fifty-eighth chapter: Pārvatī's bathing in a lake after obtaining the boon from Brahmā in order to shed her dark complexion; the emergence of Kauśikī from the bodily sheath of Pārvatī who had bathed in the lake; Kauśikī's dwelling on the peak of the Vindhya under the name Durgā by command of the Goddess.
In the fifty-ninth chapter:

7.20.s: pārvatyā giriśikharavṛkṣāgniparicārikādibhyo varadānam . tato vanadevatābhirvanditāyā devyā agniṃ pradakṣiṇī- kṛtya ṛṣīnabhivandya somanandinā sārdhaṃ viyatā jagatpaterdevadevasya patyuḥpārśvegamanam .
7.20.d: पार्वत्या गिरिशिखरवृक्षाग्निपरिचारिकादिभ्यो वरदानम् . ततो वनदेवताभिर्वन्दिताया देव्या अग्निं प्रदक्षिणी- कृत्य ऋषीनभिवन्द्य सोमनन्दिना सार्धं वियता जगत्पतेर्देवदेवस्य पत्युःपार्श्वेगमनम् .
7.20.m: Pārvatī's bestowal of boons upon the mountain peak, the trees, the fire, the attendants, and others; then the Goddess, praised by the forest deities, having circumambulated the fire and bowed to the seers, goes through the sky alongside Somanandin to the side of her husband, the Lord of the Universe and God of Gods.
In the sixtieth chapter:

7.20.s: devyā kauśikī kimarthaṃ vindhyācale saṃpreṣiteti vyāsasya jijñāsā . prasaṃgād vindhyakṛtādityamārgāvarodhanāgastyakṛta tadavamānakathākhyānam. sundanisundopākhyāna prasaṃgena gokarṇakṣetrotpattyākhyānam . gokarṇe sundanisundayo- stapaścaryā, brahmaṇaḥ sakāśād varaprāptiḥ .
7.20.d: देव्या कौशिकी किमर्थं विन्ध्याचले संप्रेषितेति व्यासस्य जिज्ञासा . प्रसंगाद् विन्ध्यकृतादित्यमार्गावरोधनागस्त्यकृत तदवमानकथाख्यानम्. सुन्दनिसुन्दोपाख्यान प्रसंगेन गोकर्णक्षेत्रोत्पत्त्याख्यानम् . गोकर्णे सुन्दनिसुन्दयो- स्तपश्चर्या, ब्रह्मणः सकाशाद् वरप्राप्तिः .
7.20.m: Vyāsa's inquiry as to why Kauśikī was sent to Mount Vindhya; in that connection, the story of the obstruction of the sun's path by the Vindhya and its subjugation by Agastya; the account of the origin of the sacred field of Gokarṇa in the context of the episode of Sunda and Upasunda; the practice of austerity by Sunda and Upasunda at Gokarṇa, and the attainment of a boon from Brahmā.
In the sixty-first chapter:

7.20.s: varadṛptayoḥ sundanisundayorlokanāśāya nirgamaḥ. atyācāraḥ, nandanavanāvamardanam . amarāvatīpraveśañca, devānāṃ tataḥ pūrvameva palāyanam .
7.20.d: वरदृप्तयोः सुन्दनिसुन्दयोर्लोकनाशाय निर्गमः. अत्याचारः, नन्दनवनावमर्दनम् . अमरावतीप्रवेशञ्च, देवानां ततः पूर्वमेव पलायनम् .
7.20.m: Departure of Sunda and Upasunda, arrogant from their boons, to destroy the worlds; their outrage, the devastation of the Nandana grove, and their entry into Amarāvatī, the gods having already fled beforehand.
In the sixty-second chapter:

7.20.s: amarāvatīṃ vijitavatoḥ sundanisundayorvindhyācale nivasanam . tayoḥ saṃhārāya devānāṃ tilottamāsarjanam . tāṃ prati śivasyānugrahaḥ, maṇḍaleśvarasamākhyā . piṇḍāreśvarotpattiḥ, tilottamāyā vindhyācale gamanam . sunda- nisundayostilottamādarśanam . tilottamārthaṃ kalahāyamānayoḥ kāmasamūḍhacetasoḥ sundanindayoḥ parasparagadāprahāreṇa nidhanam . sundanisundayormṛtayorjīvataḥ śuṃbhaniśuṃbhotpattiḥ . tayostapaścarmā, varaprāptiḥ, devadānavasaṃgaraḥ, śuṃbha- niśuṃbhayorvijayaśrīprāptiḥ, devānāmantardhānam .
7.20.d: अमरावतीं विजितवतोः सुन्दनिसुन्दयोर्विन्ध्याचले निवसनम् . तयोः संहाराय देवानां तिलोत्तमासर्जनम् . तां प्रति शिवस्यानुग्रहः, मण्डलेश्वरसमाख्या . पिण्डारेश्वरोत्पत्तिः, तिलोत्तमाया विन्ध्याचले गमनम् . सुन्द- निसुन्दयोस्तिलोत्तमादर्शनम् . तिलोत्तमार्थं कलहायमानयोः कामसमूढचेतसोः सुन्दनिन्दयोः परस्परगदाप्रहारेण निधनम् . सुन्दनिसुन्दयोर्मृतयोर्जीवतः शुंभनिशुंभोत्पत्तिः . तयोस्तपश्चर्मा, वरप्राप्तिः, देवदानवसंगरः, शुंभ- निशुंभयोर्विजयश्रीप्राप्तिः, देवानामन्तर्धानम् .
7.20.m: The dwelling on Mount Vindhya of Sunda and Upasunda after conquering Amarāvatī. The gods' creation of Tilottamā for their destruction. Śiva's grace toward her, [and] the appellation Maṇḍaleśvara. The origin of Piṇḍāreśvara; Tilottamā's journey to Mount Vindhya. Sunda and Upasunda's seeing of Tilottamā. The death of Sunda and Upasunda, whose minds were bewildered by desire, by striking each other with maces while fighting over Tilottamā. The birth of Śumbha and Niśumbha while the dead Sunda and Upasunda were yet alive. Their practice of austerities, attainment of boons, the battle between the gods and the Dānavas, Śumbha and Niśumbha's attainment of the splendor of victory, [and] the disappearance of the gods.
63 In the sixty-third chapter:

7.20.s: devān vijitavatoḥ śuṃbhaniśuṃbhayorvindhyācale āgatya nivasanam . śuṃbhānucarasya mūkadānavasya vindhyaśikhare kauśikīdarśanam . mūkavacasā kāmāturasya śuṃbhasya devīsamīpe dūtapreṣaṇam . devyā svasya yuddhaśulkatvajñāpanam . daityānāmitikartavyatāviṣaye parāmarśaḥ .
7.20.d: देवान् विजितवतोः शुंभनिशुंभयोर्विन्ध्याचले आगत्य निवसनम् . शुंभानुचरस्य मूकदानवस्य विन्ध्यशिखरे कौशिकीदर्शनम् . मूकवचसा कामातुरस्य शुंभस्य देवीसमीपे दूतप्रेषणम् . देव्या स्वस्य युद्धशुल्कत्वज्ञापनम् . दैत्यानामितिकर्तव्यताविषये परामर्शः .
7.20.m: The dwelling on Mount Vindhya of Śumbha and Niśumbha after conquering the gods. The sighting of Kauśikī on the peak of the Vindhya by the Dānava Mūka, an attendant of Śumbha. The sending of an envoy to the goddess by Śumbha, who was afflicted with desire upon Mūka's words. The goddess's announcement of herself as one whose bride-price is battle. The deliberation among the Daityas regarding what ought to be done.
64 In the sixty-fourth chapter—

7.20.s: daityānāṃ sainyasannāhaḥ, śuṃbhaniśuṃbhayormahatā sainyena kauśikīṃ prati prayāṇam . devyāḥśarīrād yoginīnāṃ prādurbhāvaḥ . devyāḥ sainyasajjā, yuddhāya niryāṇam .
7.20.d: दैत्यानां सैन्यसन्नाहः, शुंभनिशुंभयोर्महता सैन्येन कौशिकीं प्रति प्रयाणम् . देव्याःशरीराद् योगिनीनां प्रादुर्भावः . देव्याः सैन्यसज्जा, युद्धाय निर्याणम् .
7.20.m: The mobilization of the army of the Daityas; the march of Śumbha and Niśumbha toward Kauśikī with a great army. The manifestation of the Yoginīs from the body of the goddess. The equipping of the goddess's army, [and] their setting forth for battle.
65 In the sixty-fifth chapter:

7.20.s: devīnāṃ daityānāṃ ca mithastumulaṃ yuddham . devīkṛtaṃ daityānāṃ kadanam . ṣaṣṭhīmeghasvanayoḥ mṛtyukārtasvarayorlakṣmīdrumayoḥ kāntimayayoḥ saramāmurayoścaṇḍāghanayorniyatikharayoḥ prabhāvatīdhundhvoḥ saṃsaktaṃ dvandvayuddham . yuddhe daityasainyānāṃ vināśaḥ . yudhi vihataparākramapauruṣāṇāṃ dānavayodhamukhyānāṃ dviradavarānadhiṣṭhāya punaryuddhāya prayatanam .
7.20.d: देवीनां दैत्यानां च मिथस्तुमुलं युद्धम् . देवीकृतं दैत्यानां कदनम् . षष्ठीमेघस्वनयोः मृत्युकार्तस्वरयोर्लक्ष्मीद्रुमयोः कान्तिमययोः सरमामुरयोश्चण्डाघनयोर्नियतिखरयोः प्रभावतीधुन्ध्वोः संसक्तं द्वन्द्वयुद्धम् . युद्धे दैत्यसैन्यानां विनाशः . युधि विहतपराक्रमपौरुषाणां दानवयोधमुख्यानां द्विरदवरानधिष्ठाय पुनर्युद्धाय प्रयतनम् .
7.20.m: The tumultuous battle between the goddesses and the Daityas. The slaughter of the Daityas wrought by the goddess. The single combats joined between Ṣaṣṭhī and Meghasvana, Mṛtyu and Kārtasvara, Lakṣmī and Druma, Kāntimatī and Maya, Saramā and Mura, Caṇḍā and Ghana, Niyati and Khara, [and] Prabhāvatī and Dhundhu. The destruction of the Daitya armies in battle. The effort of the foremost Dānava warriors, whose valor and manly prowess had been shattered in battle, to fight once more after mounting excellent elephants.
66 In the sixty-sixth chapter—

7.20.s: daityānāṃ prayatnaṃ viditvā devīnāmapi yuddhārthaṃ sāṃgrāmikagajottamādhirohaṇam . gajārūḍhānāṃ devīdānavānāṃ saṃkulaṃ yuddham . devībhirājau svabalānyabhyarditāni dṛṣṭvā caturaṅgiṇyā senayā śuṃbhaniśuṃbhayoḥ samājabhūmāvāgamanam . devyā saha śuṃbhaniśuṃbhayoryuddham, tumulaḥ saṃgharṣaḥ, devyā daityasainyānāmalpāvaśeṣīkaraṇam . devyā śuṃbhaniśuṃbhayordhvajakavacā- śvasārathīnāṃ nirṇāśanam . divamutpatitayoḥ śuṃbhaniśuṃbhayordevyā grīvayoḥ saṃpragṛhyā niṣpeṣaṇam, śuṃbhaniśuṃbhavadhaḥ .
7.20.d: दैत्यानां प्रयत्नं विदित्वा देवीनामपि युद्धार्थं सांग्रामिकगजोत्तमाधिरोहणम् . गजारूढानां देवीदानवानां संकुलं युद्धम् . देवीभिराजौ स्वबलान्यभ्यर्दितानि दृष्ट्वा चतुरङ्गिण्या सेनया शुंभनिशुंभयोः समाजभूमावागमनम् . देव्या सह शुंभनिशुंभयोर्युद्धम्, तुमुलः संघर्षः, देव्या दैत्यसैन्यानामल्पावशेषीकरणम् . देव्या शुंभनिशुंभयोर्ध्वजकवचा- श्वसारथीनां निर्णाशनम् . दिवमुत्पतितयोः शुंभनिशुंभयोर्देव्या ग्रीवयोः संप्रगृह्या निष्पेषणम्, शुंभनिशुंभवधः .
7.20.m: The goddesses mounting excellent war-elephants for battle after knowing the effort of the Daityas. The confused melee of the elephant-mounted goddesses and Dānavas. Śumbha and Niśumbha coming to the assembly grounds with a fourfold army upon seeing their forces crushed in battle by the goddesses. The battle of Śumbha and Niśumbha with the goddess; the tumultuous clash; the Daitya armies reduced to a small remnant by the goddess. The destruction of the banners, armor, horses, and charioteers of Śumbha and Niśumbha by the goddess. The goddess seizing by their necks and crushing Śumbha and Niśumbha as they flew into the sky; the slaying of Śumbha and Niśumbha.
67 In the sixty-seventh chapter—

7.20.s: devaiḥ kṛtā kauśikīstutiḥ, devadevyoḥ kauśikyai varapradānam . kauśikīvijayamahotsavaḥ, vindhyaśikhare devairdihitaḥ kauśikyā abhiṣekaḥ, śakravākyam .
7.20.d: देवैः कृता कौशिकीस्तुतिः, देवदेव्योः कौशिक्यै वरप्रदानम् . कौशिकीविजयमहोत्सवः, विन्ध्यशिखरे देवैर्दिहितः कौशिक्या अभिषेकः, शक्रवाक्यम् .
7.20.m: The hymn of praise to Kauśikī offered by the gods; the bestowing of a boon upon Kauśikī by the God of gods. The great festival of Kauśikī's victory; the consecration of Kauśikī performed by the gods on the peak of the Vindhya; the speech of Śakra.
68 In the sixty-eighth chapter—

7.20.s: kauśikyā svadehodbhūtānāṃ devīnāṃ laṅkādideśeṣu pratiṣṭhāpanam, kauśikīkṛto mahiṣavadhaḥ .
7.20.d: कौशिक्या स्वदेहोद्भूतानां देवीनां लङ्कादिदेशेषु प्रतिष्ठापनम्, कौशिकीकृतो महिषवधः .
7.20.m: The installation by Kauśikī of the goddesses who arose from her own body in lands such as Laṅkā; the slaying of Mahiṣa performed by Kauśikī.
69 In the sixty-ninth chapter—

7.20.s: pārvatyā gauravarṇatāsādanānantaraṃ bhartturdarśanāya himavacchiravarānmandarācale pratyāgamanam . nandikṛtā gaurīstutiḥ . vyāghradvitīyāyā gauryā bharttuścaraṇābhivandanam . gauryā devadevasya savidhe svatapaścaryāvaṇiraṇakathanam . śivena somanandino varapradānam . somasya sagaṇasya śambhorgauryāstapasthaladarśanāya himavacchikharagamanam . gaurīśikhara- samākhyā, śivena himavato varapradānam . gorīśilāstanakuṇḍālaṅkāradhārā kośīnīlakuṇḍaniścīrāgrāraṇyakṛṣṇā- jinādimahimasamākhyānam .
7.20.d: पार्वत्या गौरवर्णतासादनानन्तरं भर्त्तुर्दर्शनाय हिमवच्छिरवरान्मन्दराचले प्रत्यागमनम् . नन्दिकृता गौरीस्तुतिः . व्याघ्रद्वितीयाया गौर्या भर्त्तुश्चरणाभिवन्दनम् . गौर्या देवदेवस्य सविधे स्वतपश्चर्यावणिरणकथनम् . शिवेन सोमनन्दिनो वरप्रदानम् . सोमस्य सगणस्य शम्भोर्गौर्यास्तपस्थलदर्शनाय हिमवच्छिखरगमनम् . गौरीशिखर- समाख्या, शिवेन हिमवतो वरप्रदानम् . गोरीशिलास्तनकुण्डालङ्कारधारा कोशीनीलकुण्डनिश्चीराग्रारण्यकृष्णा- जिनादिमहिमसमाख्यानम् .
7.20.m: Pārvatī's return to Mount Mandara from the supreme peak of the Himālaya to see her husband after attaining a fair complexion. The praise of Gaurī by Nandin. Gaurī, accompanied by a tiger, saluting her husband's feet. Gaurī's recital of the narration of her austerities in the presence of the God of gods. The bestowing of a boon by Śiva upon Somanandin. Śambhu, accompanied by the Moon and his attendants, going to the peak of the Himālaya to see the site of Gaurī's austerities. The naming of Gaurīśikhara; the granting of a boon to Himavat by Śiva. The recounting of the greatness of the Gaurīśilā, Stanakuṇḍa, Alaṅkāradhārā, Kośī, Nīlakuṇḍa, Niścīrāgrāraṇya, Kṛṣṇājina, and other places.
70 In the seventieth chapter—

7.20.s: devadevasya darśanārthaṃ śakraśaśivāyūnāṃ mandarācale āgamanam . hiraṇyakaśiporvadhārthaṃ gṛhītanarasiṃharūpasya viṣṇo ruddhārārthaṃ devadevasya samīpe śakrasya prārthanā . devadevānugraheṇa vāyormūrttattvam . śaśino yakṣmāpahānāya prabhāse tapaścaraṇopadeśaḥ, prasaṃgāgataṃ hiraṇyakaśipūpākhyānam . hiraṇyakaśiporutpattiḥ, śrīparvate hiraṇyakaśipostapaścaryā . brahmaṇo varalābhaḥ, trailokyarājyakaraṇam, śrīparvatopākhyānam . śrīparvatamāhātmyam, śrīgirervarapradānam .
7.20.d: देवदेवस्य दर्शनार्थं शक्रशशिवायूनां मन्दराचले आगमनम् . हिरण्यकशिपोर्वधार्थं गृहीतनरसिंहरूपस्य विष्णो रुद्धारार्थं देवदेवस्य समीपे शक्रस्य प्रार्थना . देवदेवानुग्रहेण वायोर्मूर्त्तत्त्वम् . शशिनो यक्ष्मापहानाय प्रभासे तपश्चरणोपदेशः, प्रसंगागतं हिरण्यकशिपूपाख्यानम् . हिरण्यकशिपोरुत्पत्तिः, श्रीपर्वते हिरण्यकशिपोस्तपश्चर्या . ब्रह्मणो वरलाभः, त्रैलोक्यराज्यकरणम्, श्रीपर्वतोपाख्यानम् . श्रीपर्वतमाहात्म्यम्, श्रीगिरेर्वरप्रदानम् .
7.20.m: The arrival of Śakra, the Moon, and the Wind on Mount Mandara to see the God of gods. Śakra's petition before the God of gods for the relief of Viṣṇu, who had assumed the form of Narasiṃha to slay Hiraṇyakaśipu. The Wind attaining embodied form through the grace of the God of gods. The instruction for the Moon to perform austerities at Prabhāsa to dispel his consumption; the narrative of Hiraṇyakaśipu introduced in that context. The birth of Hiraṇyakaśipu; Hiraṇyakaśipu's practice of austerities on Śrīparvata. The obtaining of a boon from Brahmā; his ruling over the three worlds; the narrative of Śrīparvata. The greatness of Śrīparvata; the granting of a boon by Śrīgiri.
71 In the seventy-first chapter—

7.20.s: hiraṇyakaśiporatyācāreṇa pīḍitānāṃ devānāṃ brahmaṇā saha viṣṇoḥ samīpe gamanam . hiraṇyakaśiporvadhārthaṃ prārthanā, viṣṇunā narasiṃharūpeṇa hiraṇyakaśiporvadhaḥ . rudrasya śarabharūpeṇāvatāraḥ, nṛsiṃhakṛtā śarabhastutiḥ . śarabharūpiṇā rudreṇa viṣṇornṛsiṃharūpātsamuddharaṇam .
7.20.d: हिरण्यकशिपोरत्याचारेण पीडितानां देवानां ब्रह्मणा सह विष्णोः समीपे गमनम् . हिरण्यकशिपोर्वधार्थं प्रार्थना, विष्णुना नरसिंहरूपेण हिरण्यकशिपोर्वधः . रुद्रस्य शरभरूपेणावतारः, नृसिंहकृता शरभस्तुतिः . शरभरूपिणा रुद्रेण विष्णोर्नृसिंहरूपात्समुद्धरणम् .
7.20.m: The gods, afflicted by the atrocities of Hiraṇyakaśipu, going into the presence of Viṣṇu along with Brahmā. The petition for the slaying of Hiraṇyakaśipu; the slaying of Hiraṇyakaśipu by Viṣṇu in the form of Narasiṃha. Rudra's descent in the form of Śarabha; the hymn of praise to Śarabha offered by Nṛsiṃha. The rescue of Viṣṇu from the form of Nṛsiṃha by Rudra in the form of Śarabha.
72 In the seventy-second chapter—

7.20.s: mandare viharato devadevasya pārvatyāḥ prārthanayā vindhyācalamāgamya tatra manasā nirmite mahāpure yogasandhānamāsthāya tayā saha mahāsuratārambhaḥ . tannimittāt mahotpātān dṛṣṭvā bhītairdevairvindhyamāgatya śaṃkaradarśanārthaṃ tatsavidhe lakṣyadūtarūpeṇa vahneḥ preṣaṇam . tatra nandino'nugraheṇa vahnerabhyantarapraveśaḥ . vahneḥ prārthanayā devadevasya mahāsuratā- ttūṣṇīṃ niṣkramya devebhyo darśanadānam . devyāstanayayogāpanodanāya śambhoḥ suratavirataye devānāṃ prārthanā . devānāṃ tuṣṭyartha śambhunā cirasandhāritasya svatejaso vahnāvādhānam . mahāsuratabhaṅgāt pārvatyāḥ prakopaḥ . nandinaṃ prati roṣeṇa karṇotpalaprakṣepaḥ . tataḥ svarṇaśṛṃgasamīpato bhadrotpalasarotpattiḥ . devatābhyaḥ pārvatyāḥ śāpaḥ . kaiṭabha nāmnā pārvatyāstatrāvasthānam . ramaṇaśilāmahimā, śaṅkarasakāśe devānāmandhakatapaḥpravṛttivijñāpanam . śaṃkareṇa devānāṃ samāśvāsanam, śaṃkarājñayā māheśvatejasau devaiḥ śaravaṇe samutsarjanam . tatprabhāvāt tatra sarvasya hiraṇmayībhāvaḥ .
